title: Each record is one row of its kind's table, one line of its file
statement: Each record MUST be one row of its kind's table, with typed columns, kept as one line of `data/<table>.jsonl`; its parts and its links MUST be rows of their own tables. The data files MUST be the source of truth: nothing else MAY hold a record's content, and the database built from them is never committed.

title: A rule or requirement states its rule in full in its statement
statement: The statement of a domain rule or requirement SHOULD state the rule in full using MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD or MAY. The title MUST be the rule in a few words.

title: Line and column order do not change what a data file means
statement: Reordering the lines of a data file, or the columns of a line, MUST NOT change what the data means: a record's product, domain, parent and links come only from its columns and its relations' rows. A file in the data folder that is not a `.jsonl` file MUST be ignored.

title: A record can point at the code that builds or proves it
statement: A component MUST be able to name its `file`, and a test the `file` that runs it, each as a path relative to the repo root.

title: Every writer uses the same commands
statement: The CLI, the plugin's MCP tools and the app MUST all change data through the same commands, `add`, `set`, `move`, `link`, `unlink` and `remove`, each one write through the command layer, with `show`, `list` and `next-id` to read the data.

title: Commands take their columns from the schema
statement: The CLI's flags and help, and the MCP tools' input schemas, MUST be generated from the schema description, product kinds included, so a new column needs no change to any writer. A flag that is no column, or a value of the wrong type, MUST be refused as bad usage.

title: A refused write says every reason and changes nothing
statement: When the command layer refuses a write, the CLI MUST print every reason with the rule it broke and exit with an error, and an MCP tool MUST return the refusal with its reasons; no data file MAY change.

title: The plugin's skills write only through the tools
statement: The plugin's skills MUST tell the Agent to change data only through the MCP tools or the CLI, never by editing data files, and every example in them MUST name real tables, columns and relations, with values of the columns' types.

title: The reference says what a domain is
statement: The domain table's description in the schema, shown in the reference, MUST say that a domain is one business capability, never a technology layer, and the `domain-named-for-technology` check's explanation MUST say that a domain is a vertical slice of business capability whose technology is a layer inside its Design stage.

title: The modeling skill finds the capabilities first
statement: The plugin's modeling skill MUST start, before any record is written, by finding the product's business capabilities and making each one a domain, and MUST list the questions that tell a capability from a technology layer.

title: A schema change takes effect on the next load
statement: A new migration MUST take effect on the next load with no other code change: the store applies the migrations in order, records them, and reads the schema back from the database.

title: Existing data is checked against the changed schema
statement: After a schema change, every product's data MUST be loaded against the new schema, so that a change which breaks existing data shows as `data-refused` errors straight away, and a change that would leave rows without a table is refused.

title: The row types and the reference follow the schema
statement: The row types in `lathe/src/store/tables.ts` and the committed reference MUST be generated from the schema, and a test MUST fail when either differs from what the schema gives.

title: A product kind gets a table of its own
statement: A product_kind row MUST give the product a table named after the kind, with an ID, a title, a required column for its parent kind and a column for each of its fields, typed and required as declared; an obligation kind MUST join the obligation supertype.

title: A product kind keeps its own label, stage, folder and obligation
statement: A product kind MUST be listed after Lathe's kinds, with its own label, stage, folder and obligation, and MUST NOT change any of Lathe's kinds.

title: A product relation adds a link table or a pair
statement: A product_relation with a new name MUST get a link table of its own; one with Lathe's name MUST add only its pair, and MUST change nothing else of that relation.

title: A kind declared twice is refused, naming its file and line
statement: Two product_kind rows with the same name MUST be refused by the store, naming the file and line of the second and the line of the first.

title: A capability sits under a domain with a whole-number position
statement: A capability MUST sit under a domain and MUST give its place in the domain in a required `position`. A use case, flow or test MAY sit under either a domain or one of its capabilities.

title: A record under a capability belongs to the capability's domain
statement: A record under a capability, and every record below it, MUST belong to the capability's domain, so that its obligations count in that domain's coverage exactly as they did directly under the domain.

title: A bad or repeated capability position is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a capability whose position is not a whole number, and one whose position another capability of the same domain has, naming the other. Capabilities in different domains MAY share a position.

title: A use case left outside the capabilities is a warning
statement: When a domain has at least one capability, the engine MUST report a `use-case-outside-capability` warning for each of its use cases that sits directly under the domain. A domain with no capabilities MUST NOT be reported.

title: A pattern sits under the product and use cases or domains follow it
statement: A pattern MUST sit under a product and MAY list its settings as pattern_setting rows. A use case, or a domain, MAY follow one or more patterns with the `follows` relation.

title: A follower that does not answer a pattern setting is an error
statement: For each pattern a use case follows and each of the pattern's settings, the use case MUST have a setting_value row with a value or a not-applicable reason; otherwise `pattern-setting-missing` MUST report an error. A not-applicable answer MUST give its reason.

title: Two followed patterns may share a setting name
statement: When a use case follows two patterns that both have a setting of one name, it MUST answer each pattern's setting with its own setting_value row, and neither MAY be reported.

title: A pattern setting that is not a lower-case name is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a pattern_setting whose name is not lower-case letters, digits and underscores starting with a letter. Any such name, `title` included, MAY be a setting, since a setting is never a column of its follower.

title: A pattern rule may apply only for some values of a setting
statement: A pattern rule MAY apply only when one of its pattern's settings has, or has not, a value, given whole as `applies_when_setting`, `applies_when_negated` and `applies_when_value`. The store MUST refuse a condition given in part, or one naming a setting its pattern lacks.

title: A flow step sits under a flow, has a position and its own links
statement: The schema MUST have a `flow_step` kind whose parent is a `flow`, with a required `position` and `path`, and MUST allow a step to `fulfills` a requirement, an interaction requirement, a domain rule or a pattern rule, and to `uses` a view, an endpoint or a component.

title: A step position that is not a whole number is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a flow step whose `position` is not a whole number, or that has none, naming its file and line.

title: Two steps on one path with the same position are refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a second step on the same path of the same flow with the same position. Steps of different flows, or on different paths of one flow, MAY share a position.

title: A step fulfilling something its flow does not carry out is a warning
statement: A step that `fulfills` a record that is not a requirement of a use case its flow `carries_out`, a domain rule one of those use cases `applies`, or an interaction requirement that fulfills one of those or sits under the flow, MUST be reported as a `flow-step-fulfills-outside-flow` warning naming the target and the use cases compared.

title: A flow with steps that fulfills something none of its steps does is a warning
statement: A flow that has steps and `fulfills` a record that none of its steps fulfills MUST be reported as a `flow-fulfills-differs-from-steps` warning naming that record.

title: A flow may leave fulfills to its steps; one without steps is not compared
statement: A flow with steps MUST NOT be reported for leaving out, or for repeating, links its steps already have. A flow without steps MUST NOT be compared with steps.

title: An ID in text is kept as written and makes no link
statement: The engine MUST keep a record's text exactly as written, IDs, repeats, its own ID, code spans and fences included, and MUST NOT read a link, a mention or any other relation from it.

title: No check reads text for IDs
statement: Checks MUST NOT report an ID in text, whether a record has it or not and whatever its prefix; the engine's one problem of its own is `data-refused`.

title: The engine loads the folders and each kind's folder
statement: The engine MUST load each kind's folder and the schema's folders into `Workspace.sections`, the stages' folders by position and then the product-level ones. A kind with no folder MUST sit in none.

title: A product places its own kinds in the schema's folders
statement: A product kind MAY name one of the schema's folders as its section, and MUST NOT add or change a folder or move one of Lathe's kinds.

title: A kind in a folder that is not listed is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a product kind whose section names no folder of the schema, naming the folder.

title: A kind in another stage's folder is an error
statement: A kind whose folder belongs to a stage other than the kind's own MUST be a `section-stage-mismatch` error naming the kind, its stage and the folder's stage. A folder of no stage, such as `shared`, MUST NOT be reported for any kind.

title: The schema has layers that hold components
statement: The schema MUST have a `layer` kind that sits under a domain or a layer in the Technical specification folder with a required `position`, and MUST let a `component` or a technical flow sit under a domain or a layer. No other kind MAY sit under a layer.

title: A bad or repeated layer position is an error
statement: The store MUST refuse a layer whose position is not a whole number, and `layer-order` MUST report as an error each layer whose position another layer with the same parent also has, naming the parent and the other layers. Layers in different domains MUST NOT be compared.

title: A component outside its domain's layers is a warning
statement: A component that sits directly under a domain that has at least one layer MUST be a `component-outside-layer` warning naming the component and the domain. A component in a domain with no layers, and a component in a layer, MUST NOT be reported.

title: A component in a layer belongs to the layer's domain
statement: A component under a layer MUST have the layer's domain and product as its own, and coverage MUST count what it designs and builds in that domain, as it counts a component directly under the domain.

title: Every check judges a layered component as one in the domain
statement: Every check that judges a component by its domain, such as the coverage, owed pattern rule, proof and flow step checks, MUST report a domain whose components sit in layers exactly as the same domain with its components directly under it.

title: An entity's kind and links are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have an `entity` kind in the domain model folder, under an aggregate and requiring `role`, the relations `has_one`, `has_many` and `refers_to` from entity to entity, and `involves` from domain rule to aggregate, labeled Involves and Involved in. The reference MUST describe them, and when a domain rule sits under its domain.

title: An entity's fields are its entity_field rows
statement: The engine MUST give each entity its entity_field rows as its fields, in position order, each with its name, meaning, type and example; other kinds MUST have none.

title: A role other than root or child is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse an entity whose `role` is not root or child, or that has none, naming its file and line.

title: An aggregate without exactly one root is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse an aggregate with entities but no root, or with more than one, naming the aggregate and how many roots it has.

title: An entity without fields is an error, and a bad field is refused
statement: An entity with no fields MUST be an `entity-fields` error that names the fix. The store MUST refuse a field without a name, a meaning or a type, and a name used twice in one entity, compared trimmed and in any letter case.

title: A part outside its aggregate is an error
statement: A `has_one` or `has_many` to an entity in another aggregate MUST be a `has-crosses-aggregate` error that says to use `refers_to` or move the part. A `refers_to` across aggregates or domains MUST NOT be reported.

title: A child its root does not reach is a warning
statement: A child entity that no `has_one` or `has_many` reaches from its aggregate's root, directly or through other children, MUST be an `entity-unreferenced` warning. An aggregate without exactly one root MUST NOT have its children judged.

title: The reference script prints the reference, or writes it to a file
statement: The reference script (`npm --prefix lathe run reference`) MUST write the reference as Markdown: how data is kept, then the kinds with their tables, the other tables, the relations, the folders and the checks, each with its own anchor. With `--print` it MUST print it, and with `--out <file>` write it to that file.

title: The reference gives every fact of each kind, table, relation, folder and check
statement: The reference MUST give each kind's label, description, stage, folder, parents and children, obligation and ID convention; each table's role, keys and columns with their types, values, references and descriptions; each relation's role, labels, description and pairs; each folder's stage, position, label and description; and each check's name, severity, summary, explanation and kinds. The engine's own problem, `data-refused`, MUST be listed as a check too.

title: A product's reference shows its own kinds and its own checks
statement: The reference MUST be the product's own: its kinds, tables and relations with its declarations, and its own checks after Lathe's and the engine's.

title: GET /api/reference serves the reference
statement: The API MUST serve the product's reference as JSON at `GET /api/reference`, and refuse any other method.

title: Lathe's committed reference never goes stale
statement: Lathe's reference MUST be committed as `lathe/REFERENCE.md`, so an agent can read it without running anything. The package build MUST regenerate it, and a test MUST fail when the committed file differs from what the reference script writes.

title: What the reference would leave blank is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a product kind or relation without a description, and a check row without its summary or explanation; Lathe's own tables, kinds and checks MUST all be described.

title: Relations read in plain words from both ends
statement: Each relation MUST carry a `forward_label`, the link read from its source ("Satisfies"), and a `reverse_label`, the link read from its target ("Designed by"), in sentence case. The reference MUST show both and list each kind's links out by their forward labels and its links in by their reverse labels. The store MUST refuse a product relation without both.

title: A domain event's kind and links are in the schema
statement:
The schema MUST have a `domain_event` kind in the domain model folder, under an aggregate, with IDs `

--EV`, the relation `raised_by` from domain event to entity, and `reacts_to` from an aggregate, a use case or a component to a domain event. The reference MUST describe them.

title: An event's fields are its event_field rows, checked as an entity's
statement: The engine MUST give each domain event its event_field rows as its fields. `entity-fields` MUST report an event with no fields as it does an entity, naming the record as an event, and the store MUST refuse a field without a name, or named twice.

title: A raised_by outside the event's aggregate is an error
statement: A `raised_by` link to an entity that sits in another aggregate than the event MUST be a `raised-by-outside-aggregate` error that names both aggregates and the fix. An event with no `raised_by` MUST NOT be reported.

title: An event nothing reacts to is a warning
statement: A domain event that no record links to with `reacts_to` MUST be an `event-unheard` warning that says this can be fine and suggests the aggregate, use case or component that might react.

title: A title that does not read as past tense is a warning
statement: A domain event whose title has no past form as its last word or after its first, by a heuristic of "-ed" endings and a documented list of irregular past forms kept in the check, MUST be an `event-tense` warning.

title: A flow's steps are numbered within their path
statement: A flow step MAY name its `path`, a short name such as main or refused; a step written without one MUST be on the main path. Within each path of a flow the steps' positions MUST be whole numbers, unique and without gaps: the store refuses a repeated or broken position, and `step-order` reports a gap as an error.

title: A domain rule may sit under an entity, and a layer under a layer
statement: A domain rule MAY sit under an entity, and a layer MAY sit under another layer. Coverage, the structure checks and every check that reads a record's domain MUST treat these records as they treat the same records one level up.

title: Requirements, interaction requirements, pattern rules and standard rules may name a group
statement: A `requirement`, `interaction_requirement`, `pattern_rule` or `standard_rule` MAY name a short heading in `group_name`, such as Validation or Paging, so that a long list of them is sorted under headings as a real product sorts it. Groups MUST be compared trimmed and in any letter case. A group is a column, not a record, so renaming one MUST change no ID.

title: The format page says how records are kept, then indexes kinds, relations and checks
statement: The format page (`/format`) MUST say how records are kept, then show an index: the kinds by stage and by folder within each stage, the relations with their words read both ways, and the checks under Errors and Warnings. Kinds and checks MUST be clickable rows leading to their pages.

title: A kind page shows everything the reference says about the kind, with a real example
statement: A kind's page (`/format/kinds/<kind>`) MUST show its description; its stage and folder; its allowed parents and children as links to their kind pages; its columns, each with its type, whether it is required, its meaning and its own anchor; its obligation and its ID convention; the relations out of it and into it by their readable labels, each naming the kind at the other end; and the checks that concern it. It MUST show the product's first record of the kind with a link to it, and the count of the product's records of the kind, with a row per parent leading to that parent's group of them.

title: A check page shows its explanation, its query and the problems it reports now
statement: A check's page (`/format/checks/<check>`) MUST show its severity, its summary and explanation (rendered Markdown), where it comes from and its query, the kinds it concerns, and the current space's problems with that code as clickable rows.

title: Format pages open in the workbench, with the side bar showing the facts
statement: Each format page MUST open as any other page does: one pane with the page's title in it, and the side bar beside it (a bottom sheet on a phone) showing the kind's or the check's facts, shown and hidden with the same toggle and command as on a record page.

title: Kinds, problem codes and columns link to their format pages
statement: The side bar's Kind row MUST link to the kind's page, on a record page and on a group page. Every problem's code on the Checks page, the domain page and the record page MUST link to its check's page. A record's column labels MUST link to that column on its kind's page.

title: The record format is a command and a link in the shortcuts sheet
statement: The record format MUST NOT be a link in the nav's footer or rail. It MUST be the "Record format" command in the command palette (g then f) and a link in the shortcuts sheet; the desktop app's Help menu has an entry too. The footer MUST keep saying where the data comes from.

title: Quick find finds kinds and checks
statement: Quick find MUST list every kind as "Kind: <label>" and every check as "Check: <name>", found by their names and labels, each leading to its page.

title: A record's data file can be revealed, opened in the editor and its ID copied
statement: In the desktop app a record's facts MUST offer Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID for the data file that holds its row, and a right-click on a record row, a graph node or a record page's title MUST open a native menu of the same three. In a browser the app MUST show none of them.

title: Open in editor uses VS Code unless another editor is chosen
statement: Open in editor MUST open the record's data file in VS Code by default; File › Open Records In MUST offer Cursor, Zed, the system's default app and a command of the Owner's own from `settings.json`.

title: Standards and meets are in the schema
statement:
The schema MUST have a `standard` kind under the product and a `standard_rule` kind under a standard, both in the Shared folder right after the patterns, with IDs `

-STD-` and `-R`, and the relation `meets` from a component, a technical step or a test to a standard rule, labeled Meets and Met by, with no role. The reference MUST describe them, with the rule of thumb that a rule you prove with tests is a pattern rule and a rule you follow and meet is a standard rule.

title: A standard rule owes no coverage
statement: Coverage MUST NOT count a standard rule in any domain, and no check MUST report one as not designed or not proved. An ID of a standard rule in text MUST be plain text, never a link.

title: A standard rule nothing meets is a warning
statement: `lathe check` MUST report a `standard-rule-unmet` warning for each standard rule that no record meets, naming it in text not counting. The message MUST say how to link what follows the rule.

title: Standards sit under Shared, each listing its rules and what meets them
statement: The nav MUST list a product's standards in its Shared folder beside its patterns. A standard's page MUST list its rules in a table, one row each, with what meets each rule, and say when nothing does yet.

title: A standard rule shows what meets it
statement: A standard rule's Traceability MUST list what meets it under Met by, with no coverage gaps, and what meets it MUST list the rule under Meets. The reference MUST have a page for each standard kind, made from the schema.

title: The graph draws standards as patterns with a ruler
statement: The graph MUST draw a standard and its rules in the product's Shared folder in the Design colors, shaped as a pattern and a pattern rule with a ruler mark (`LA-EXP-DR65`), and a `meets` link as a design line, and its key MUST say so.

title: A technical flow sits in a domain or a layer and deepens a flow
statement: The schema MUST have a `design_flow` kind in Technical specification whose parent is a domain or a layer, and MUST allow it to `deepens` a flow.

title: A technical step has a position and path, and may name its transaction
statement: The schema MUST have a `design_step` kind whose parent is a technical flow, with a required `position` and `path`; a step MAY give `transaction_name`, `locks` and `statements`, and the workspace MUST keep them as its columns.

title: A technical step uses a component and satisfies obligations
statement: The schema MUST allow a technical step to `uses` a component, and to `satisfies` a requirement, a domain rule, an interaction requirement or a pattern rule.

title: A technical step's satisfies counts as design
statement: Coverage MUST count an obligation a technical step satisfies as designed, and MUST NOT count it as built unless a component whose file exists satisfies it; `unsatisfied` MUST NOT report it.

title: A technical step's position is checked on its path
statement: The store MUST refuse a technical step whose `position` is not a whole number, that has none or that another step on its path has; `step-order` MUST report a path whose positions skip a number, worded for a technical step, as a flow's steps are.

title: A technical flow that deepens nothing is a warning
statement: A technical flow with no `deepens` link MUST be reported as a `design-flow-deepens-nothing` warning naming it.

title: An API sits in a domain and holds its endpoints and the rules they share
statement: The schema MUST have an `api` kind in Interaction design whose parent is a domain, MUST allow an `endpoint` under an API or a domain, and MUST allow an `interaction_requirement` under an API.

title: An integration holds one interaction requirement per exchange
statement: The schema MUST have an `integration` kind in Interaction design whose parent is a domain, with an optional `system` column, and MUST allow an `interaction_requirement` under it.

title: An interaction requirement may sit directly under the domain
statement: The schema MUST allow an `interaction_requirement` directly under a domain, for a rule shared across the domain's interaction design, and it MUST count as an obligation of that domain.

title: Both sides' rows are kept, sorted
statement: The merge driver MUST keep the rows each side added, and a change or a removal made on one side only, keep one copy of a row both sides added alike, and write the merged file sorted by key.

title: A real clash fails the merge, naming it
statement: The merge driver MUST fail, exiting 1 and naming the clash, when one key is added on both sides with different content, or one row is changed on both sides or removed on one and changed on the other.

title: The merged table's own rules are checked
statement: The merge driver MUST check the merged file against its table's own rules (columns, types, keys and checks) and fail on a row that breaks them; keys to other tables MUST be checked when the data next loads.

title: Git runs the driver for every data file
statement: The merge driver MUST run as `lathe merge-data %O %A %B %P` for every file `.gitattributes` names with `merge=lathe-data`, writing the merge over ours as git expects.

title: The check prints errors, then warnings, then coverage
statement: `lathe check` MUST print every error, then every warning, then one coverage line per domain. Each coverage line MUST show, for requirements and for domain rules, how many are designed, built and proved out of the total.

title: The check exits non-zero on any error
statement: `lathe check` MUST exit with status 1 when there is at least one error, and with status 0 otherwise. Warnings MUST NOT change the exit status.

title: The check can print the whole workspace as JSON
statement: With `--json`, `lathe check` MUST print the whole `Workspace` as JSON instead of the text report.

title: Data that breaks the schema is refused, and is an error
statement: The store MUST refuse each row that breaks the schema (a duplicate or malformed ID, an unknown column, a missing title, parent or required column, a parent or link naming a record that does not exist or of a kind not allowed, a link into another product), and `lathe check` MUST report each refusal as a `data-refused` error naming the file, the line and the rule. A check MUST report a test whose file is missing or does not name what it proves as an error naming the test.

title: A data file that does not load is an error, not a crash
statement: A data file that cannot be loaded (a line that is not JSON, a value of the wrong type, a row the schema refuses) MUST become `data-refused` errors naming the file, the line and the rule, and `lathe check` MUST report them without crashing. Nothing else MAY be checked until the data loads.

title: A new check needs only a new check row
statement: Adding a check MUST need only a new row of the `check` table, added through the command layer, such as `lathe add check`. It MUST NOT need a change to the engine's TypeScript.

title: Checks can read every typed table
statement: A check's query MUST be able to read every typed table, the `record_parent`, `record_scope` and `link` views, the `meta_*` tables and the coverage views. The file facts (`file_facts`: whether a test's or component's file exists, and whether a test's file names its ID or key; `file_mentions`: which IDs it names) MUST be filled before the checks run, so checks stay in SQL.

title: A domain rule that no use case applies is a warning
statement: A domain rule that no use case links to with `applies` MUST be reported as a `rule-not-applied` warning on that rule.

title: A use case no flow carries out is a warning once its domain has flows
statement: A use case that no flow links to with `carries_out` MUST be reported as a `use-case-without-flow` warning, but only when the use case's domain has at least one flow. A flow that only `fulfills` the use case's requirements does not carry it out.

title: An interaction requirement that fulfills nothing is a warning
statement: An interaction requirement with no `fulfills` link MUST be reported as an `interaction-requirement-fulfills-nothing` warning.

title: A test whose type does not suit what it proves is a warning
statement: A test whose `test_type` is `domain_rule` (in any letter case) and that proves requirements but no domain rule, or whose `test_type` is `acceptance` and that proves domain rules but no requirement, MUST be reported as a `test-type-mismatch` warning naming what it proves. Other test types, such as `unit`, and tests that prove both MUST NOT be reported.

title: A product relation declared twice is refused, naming the file and line
statement: The store MUST refuse a `product_relation` row with the same name, source kind and target kind as another, once, naming its file and line.

title: A duplicated ID is one refusal, not one per link to it
statement: When a row takes an ID another record already has, the store MUST refuse it once, as `unique-id`, naming the record that has the ID with its file and line, and MUST NOT refuse the links to that ID with it.

title: An unknown parent is refused once
statement: A record whose parent column names no record MUST be refused once, as a foreign key naming the missing record and the kind it must be, and nothing else MAY be reported about that parent.

title: A component that satisfies nothing is a warning
statement: A component with no `satisfies` link to an obligation that exists MUST be reported as a `component-satisfies-nothing` warning, whose message says to link what it designs or implements (for shared infrastructure, what it makes possible) or remove it.

title: A test that proves and supports nothing is a warning
statement: A test with no `proves` and no `supports` link to a record that exists MUST be reported as a `test-proves-nothing` warning, whatever its state. Running a flow or covering a component does not count.

title: A link or parent the schema does not allow is refused once
statement: The store MUST refuse a link whose target is of a kind its relation's end does not accept, naming the kinds that end accepts, and a parent column its kind does not have, each once.

title: A product's check rows run after Lathe's checks
statement: The engine MUST run every check row with the product's `product_id` after all of Lathe's checks, in `position` order, against the same tables, and MUST read the same `record`, `message` and `severity` columns from each. A product with no check rows of its own MUST run only Lathe's checks, and a product's check MUST report only on records of its product.

title: A product check's name comes from its row
statement: A product check's problems MUST be named by its row's `name`, as Lathe's checks are, whatever its query returns in a column of its own.

title: A product check named like one of Lathe's checks is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a product check row whose name one of Lathe's checks has, naming `lathe/data/check.jsonl`, so the row never runs; the same row written into a data file MUST be a `data-refused` error.

title: A product check that fails to run is an error naming the check
statement: A product check whose query fails to run MUST be reported as an error under its check name, saying that the check could not run and why, and the other checks MUST still run.

title: lathe.config.json refuses a checks setting
statement: `lathe.config.json` MUST refuse a `checks` key as an unknown setting, naming it, since a product's checks are rows of its data.

title: A record with too many children of one kind is a warning
statement: A record with more children of one kind than the product's `max_children` setting MUST be a `too-many-children` warning that names the record, the kind and the count, and says to add a level between them, such as a capability, a layer or another aggregate. Children MUST be counted per kind, and tests MUST NOT be counted.

title: The limit is the product's max_children setting, 15 by default
statement: The checks MUST read the limit from the product's `product_setting.max_children`, and use 15 when the product has no row. The store MUST refuse any value that is not a whole number of at least 1.

title: A capability or layer with one child is a warning
statement: A capability or a layer with exactly one child MUST be a `lone-child` warning that names it and its child and says to merge it into a neighbor or give it more.

title: A lone child counts the record's own children of every kind
statement: The `lone-child` check MUST count every child of the capability or layer, of any kind, and only its own children, not theirs. A capability or layer with no children, or with two or more, MUST NOT be reported.

title: A flow's steps are counted per path
statement: `too-many-children` MUST count a flow's steps per path (a step with no path is on the main path), since each path reads as its own list, and its message MUST name the path when it is not main.

title: Grouped children are counted per group
statement: `too-many-children` MUST count requirements, interaction requirements, pattern rules and standard rules per `group_name`, the ungrouped ones as one list, with groups compared trimmed and in any letter case, since each group reads under its own heading; its message MUST name the group.

title: A group with one member is a lone child
statement: A group with exactly one member MUST get a `lone-child` warning on its parent, naming the group and its member, as a capability or a layer with one child does.

title: A space's Checks page lists its product's problems, errors first, grouped by check
statement: A space's Checks page MUST list every problem of its product, errors before warnings, grouped by check, each linking to its record, then the problems that belong to no product (data the store refuses, a check that could not run) under a Workspace heading, which every space's Checks page shows. It MUST NOT list another product's problems.

title: The Dock badge counts the check errors of the product in front
statement: The Dock badge MUST show the number of check errors of the focused window's current space, its product's and the workspace's (as its Checks page counts them), follow it when the data reloads or the space changes, and show nothing when there are none.

title: A hand edit of a data file is refused and points at the tools
statement: The plugin's guard hook MUST refuse an Agent's Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit of a data file (a `.jsonl` file in the data folder `lathe.config.json` names) before it happens, saying to use Lathe's MCP tools or the `lathe` command instead.

title: Every other edit goes through silently
statement: The guard hook MUST let an edit of any other file through, with no output.

title: The plugin declares the guard hook and its scripts exist
statement: The plugin MUST declare the guard hook as a PreToolUse hook on Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit, and every script its hooks and MCP server name MUST exist.

title: The domain page groups records by stage
statement: The domain page MUST group its records by stage. Define MUST show aggregates with their rules nested, and use cases with their requirements nested. Design MUST show flows, views, endpoints, components and tests.

title: A search box filters records by ID or title
statement: The domain page MUST have a search box that filters the shown records by ID or title as the reader types.

title: The domain page shows its coverage gaps and problems
statement: The domain page MUST list the domain's coverage gaps (each with the missing link) and the problems about its records.

title: The menu lists each product and its domains
statement: The left menu MUST show each product as a space in its rail, and list the current space's domains (with their capabilities) in its panel.

title: The record page shows the whole record, field by field
statement: The record page MUST show the record's ID, kind and title; its text fields (a statement, a goal, a description, a test's Given, When and Then, notes) rendered as Markdown, a test's three as one scenario; its part rows laid out (an entity's or event's fields as a table, a use case's steps in order, a product's roles, an API's shapes); its other columns as facts; and its parent and children.

title: The record page shows links both ways, grouped by relation
statement: The record page MUST show the record's outgoing links and its incoming links, each grouped by relation, with every linked record clickable.

title: A record's text is sanitized before it is shown
statement: The HTML rendered from a record's text fields MUST be sanitized before it is put on the page, because records are written by agents as well as people.

title: The record page shows the problems about it
statement: The record page MUST list every problem whose record is this one.

title: Anywhere on a record's row opens that record
statement: In every list of records (the rows of a product, domain, record or group page, the side bar's children and members, coverage gaps, open questions, what a requirement fulfills, the patterns a domain follows, and the problems on the checks page), a click anywhere on a row MUST open the record the row leads to, not only a click on its ID or title. Cmd/Ctrl-click and middle-click MUST open it in a new tab. The row's other controls (its fold chevron, other record links, badges and buttons) MUST keep doing what they do. Keyboard focus stays on the row's one link, and its focus ring and hover cover the whole row; a tree's arrow keys work as before.

title: Record IDs named in text are links
statement: In a record's rendered text fields (a record page, and a product's or domain's overview), every ID-shaped token that is the ID of a record of the space, other than the record itself, MUST become a link to the record's address, its bare ID (`/<id>`), with the record's title on hover, and a plain click MUST move within the app. An ID inside a code block, an existing link or a code span with other text MUST NOT be linked, nor part of a longer ID; a code span holding exactly one such ID MUST link.

title: An ID that names no record stays plain text
statement: An ID-shaped token in a text field that is no record of the space MUST be shown as written, as plain text: it MUST NOT be a link, and nothing reports it, since no check reads text for IDs.

title: Depth frames levels of the nav's tree below the focus
statement: The graph view of `/<record-id>` (`?view=graph`, or its graph pane beside others) MUST show the one map of the nav's tree, stages and folders included (see LA-EXP-DR45, LA-EXP-DR57), and at depth N (1 by default, up to 3) MUST frame the record, its parent at the left edge and its descendants down to N levels below it (see LA-EXP-DR46), with no cross-links: at depth 1 its parent (or folder) and its children (or their folders). A Links switch beside Depth, off by default, MUST add the record's own links, one hop (see LA-EXP-DR49). `/graph` on its own MUST open the first product.

title: Clicking a node re-centers the graph and changes the address
statement: Clicking a record node MUST re-center the graph on that record and change the address to its graph page, so the browser's Back button walks back along the path. A breadcrumb trail MUST show the records and groups visited, named as LA-EXP-UC09-R07 says, and going back to one of them MUST cut the trail there.

title: The side bar describes the focused record
statement: The side bar MUST show the focused record's kind, title, the opening of its text, its problems and coverage gaps, the records it connects to, and an "Open page" link to the record's address, `/<id>`.

title: Node and line style show kind, relation, errors and gaps
statement: Nodes MUST be colored by stage (Define, Design, structural) and shaped by kind (see LA-EXP-DR65), a domain drawn as a hexagon (see LA-EXP-DR61), lines MUST be styled by relation, and records with errors or coverage gaps MUST carry a visible mark. A legend MUST explain the styles.

title: Kinds and relations can be switched off
statement: The reader MUST be able to hide and show each kind and each relation, and MUST be able to keep only the traceability links (satisfies, proves, fulfills) in one step.

title: The graph works from the keyboard
statement: Arrow keys or Tab MUST move between the drawn nodes, Enter MUST focus the focused record or group, and Escape MUST clear the filters and trace mode. Keyboard focus MUST always be visible.

title: Every page opens the graph in its Graph view, not from the nav
statement: Every record, group, product and domain page MUST open its graph in its own Graph view (the Graph view toggle in the page bar, Ctrl+G or Alt+G, Ctrl+2 and the command palette). The side navigation MUST NOT have a Graph item, open or as a rail: the graph is a view of a page, not a place of its own.

title: The graph is one map in columns that follow the parent/child tree
statement: The graph MUST be laid out left to right in columns by depth in the parent/child tree, one map for the product's tree (see LA-EXP-DR57): the product furthest left, then each level in its own column; the focus's ancestors to its left and its descendants to its right. Every record with the same parent, record or group, MUST sit in the same column whatever its kind (see LA-EXP-DR17). Parent/child lines MUST be drawn as the solid spine of the tree, passing through a group in its own column where the parent's children are grouped (see LA-EXP-UC04), and every other relation as a lighter, dashed cross-link. Links MUST NOT move anything: a linked record keeps its place in the map. In trace mode the graph MUST read left to right in its own columns: the requirement or rule, what fulfills it, the components, the tests, then the files.

title: Focusing moves the camera, not the map
statement: When the person focuses a record or group, the map MUST hold still: no node moves or changes size, and the camera glides, in one smooth zoom and pan on the shared motion, to frame the new focus and the levels the depth shows below it (see LA-EXP-DR59). The first picture of a page appears at once. When the system asks for reduced motion, nothing MUST animate: the camera jumps to frame the focus (see LA-EXP-DR31).

title: Hovering a node spotlights it and what it joins
statement: Hovering or keyboard-focusing a node MUST brighten it, its lines and the nodes it joins directly, and dim the rest a step; leaving MUST restore the picture. It MUST change with the motion tokens, and at once under reduced motion.

title: Edge hints count the linked records past each edge
statement: With the Links switch on, at each canvas edge a small chip MUST count the records the focus links to that lie past that edge ("3 ↑", "8 →"), update as the camera moves, and hide when nothing is past it. Clicking a chip MUST glide the camera, at its zoom, to bring the nearest of them into view, without changing the focus.

title: The keyboard steps out to the parent, in to a child and across to siblings
statement: Alt+Up MUST re-center on the parent, Alt+Down on the first child, and Alt+Shift+Left and Alt+Shift+Right on the previous and next sibling in the nav's order (Alt+Left and Alt+Right stay the browser's Back and Forward). They MUST be keymap commands, shown in the shortcuts sheet, with buttons that carry tooltips and `aria-keyshortcuts`.

title: A minimap shows the whole map and where the view sits
statement: A Minimap switch under Filters, off by default and kept per tab, MUST show a minimap in a corner: a true overview of the one map, its upper levels as boxes (as many as stay readable), the focus solid and the camera's view outlined as it moves, colored through the theme's tokens.

title: A Tree, Nested or Voronoi switch shows parents beside their children or made of them
statement: The graph's toolbar MUST offer a Layout switch of Tree, Nested and Voronoi, Tree by default, kept with the tab's graph settings (never in the address), with a command and its shortcut (`v`, which steps to the next layout) in the command list. Tree draws the one map as an icicle, each parent beside its children (`LA-EXP-DR57`). Nested draws the same tree as boxes inside boxes: the product made of its domains, a domain of Define and Design, a stage of its folders, a folder of its records (`LA-EXP-DR62`), explored by the same camera (`LA-EXP-DR63`). Voronoi draws it as polygon cells inside cells (`LA-EXP-UC03-R17`). Depth 1 to 3 frames the Tree view; the Nested and Voronoi cameras frame the focus's box or cell, so they have none, and there the Depth buttons are neither shown nor reachable, though they keep their place (`LA-EXP-DR63`). Everything else the graph does MUST work the same in all three: a click, Enter or a tap to focus, the hover spotlight with Details following it, the step keys, Tab and the arrow keys through the drawn boxes with a visible focus ring, `.` to frame the focus again, Links, Filters (a hidden kind keeps its space), trace mode, the fit and zoom buttons, the minimap, the trail, Back and Forward with the camera's glide, the side bar's Details, Outline and History, the problem and coverage marks, and the same roles and accessible names.

title: The Voronoi view shows each parent as a polygon cell made of its children's cells
statement: The Voronoi layout MUST draw the focus's product as a hexagon split into polygon cells, one per domain, each domain's cell split into Define and Design, and so on down to the records, sibling cells of equal area with the same text, each showing its own name (`LA-EXP-DR64`), so the shape of a product can be compared with its Tree and Nested pictures. It MUST share the Nested view's camera, level of detail and keyboard order (`LA-EXP-DR63`), every drawn cell showing its label inside it at the text size it shares with its siblings (`LA-EXP-DR58`, `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12`), and it MUST never keep the page waiting while it is laid out: the layout runs off the main thread, and the canvas fills once it is ready.

title: Folders and records with several kinds of children are reached through one group each
statement: The graph MUST draw the nav's stages and folders as group nodes, and when a record's children, or a folder's records, include more than one kind the nav lists side by side, MUST put a group node per kind between them, labeled with the kind's plural label and the number of members, such as "Use cases (5)". A group MUST be drawn like a folder, differently from records. The parent/child spine MUST run record, group, record, while every cross-link (satisfies, proves and so on) MUST still run record to record. Every group is a level for the depth. Hiding a kind hides its kind groups (a stage or named folder has no kind of its own), hiding the parent/child relation hides every group, and trace mode MUST show no groups.

title: A group shows its name and count, and clicking it goes to its address
statement: A group MUST show its name and count. Every member is always in the map, so there is nothing to open or fold in place, and a group has no chevron or other control of its own. Clicking the group, or pressing Enter on it, MUST go to its address, as clicking a record does.

title: A group has its own address and can be the center
statement: A group MUST be the focus at its own address: a stage or folder at `/<domain-id>/<stage>[/<folder>]`, for example `/TL-LEND/define/use-cases`, and a kind group at `/<parent-id>/<kind>`. At depth 1 the camera MUST frame its parent at the left edge and all its members to the right, and depth counts levels from it as from a record. Its side bar names the parent and lists every member. The focused record's side bar MUST link to its groups. The breadcrumb trail and the browser's Back button MUST work for groups as for records. An address for a group that does not exist MUST say so.

title: A group carries a mark when anything inside it has problems or gaps
statement: A group MUST carry the error, warning and coverage-gap marks that records carry whenever any member, or any record beneath a member, has them, so a group whose members are too small to draw still shows where the trouble is. The legend MUST explain groups and their marks.

title: Groups take their own column between a parent and its children
statement: A group MUST sit in its own column, one after its parent's and one before its members', so the graph still reads left to right. A group's siblings, and the records at the same depth under other parents, share that column.

title: The graph is a component that any page can host
statement: The graph MUST be a component that takes its focus (a record ID, or a parent ID and kind) and reports every move to a new center through a callback, without reading or changing the address itself, so a page can show it in a pane beside the record page. Its links MUST still carry a real address so they open in a new tab. It MUST fill the width and height its container gives it and frame the focus again when that size changes.

title: Domain events sit under their aggregate, and their links are dashed and labeled
statement: In the graph, an aggregate's domain events MUST sit under it through a "Domain events" group, by the one-kind rule, and each event MUST be drawn as a flag in the spark colors. With the Links switch on, an event's `reacts_to` and `raised_by` links MUST be drawn dashed in spark and labeled with their relations' labels ("Reacts to", "Raised by"); with it off they are not drawn.

title: A parent is as tall as its children, so the tree reads like an icicle
statement: In the map, a record, stage, folder or group MUST be as tall as its children stacked, each an equal part of it, and each child MUST sit right beside it, joined by a short, level parent line, so the tree reads like an icicle and no lines fan out from a parent to its children (see LA-EXP-DR57). Every node in a depth column MUST share the column's width, a fixed fraction of the map that shrinks toward the leaves, and siblings MUST share one text size, in proportion to their column's width or as large as every sibling's whole label allows, centered, the title wrapped on whole words (see LA-EXP-DR58). No node's size ever depends on what is in focus.

title: The graph shows pattern rules under their pattern and follows as a cross-link
statement: In the graph a pattern's rules MUST sit one column to its right, under it, and a use case's `follows` link MUST be drawn as a cross-link, in its own line style named in the legend; a use case reached from the pattern by that link sits one column after it. Trace mode MUST be offered for a pattern rule, showing what satisfies and proves it in every domain.

title: A record or group has one address, whatever the view
statement: A record MUST be shown at its bare ID (`/<id>`), a product and a domain included, and a group of the graph's tree at its place in it: a stage or folder at `/<domain-id>/<stage>/<folder>` (a test-plan group's parts after it, `/<domain-id>/design/test-plan/acceptance/…`), a record's kind group at `/<parent-id>/<kind>`, in every view. Any other address, the old `/records/…` and `/graph/…` addresses included, MUST show that there is no such page, and MUST stay as it was typed.

title: Wiki, Graph and Model are panes toggled on and off, named in the address
statement: A record, group, product or domain page MUST show its open views as panes side by side, always in the order Wiki, Graph, Model, as editor groups in VS Code. Wiki, Graph and Model MUST be on/off toggles, `aria-pressed` icon buttons in the View group at the right of the page bar above the panes; Model MUST be offered only on a domain, aggregate or entity page. At least one view MUST stay open: turning off the last open view MUST do nothing, and its toggle's tooltip MUST say so. Each pane's slim header MUST name its view at its left (its icon and "Wiki", "Graph" or "Model"), with, at its right, a button that closes the pane when more than one is open and its full screen button. There MUST be no Split mode and no Open beside button. The toggles and buttons MUST have a visible focus ring and their shortcut in their tooltip. The page's title MUST sit at the top of the leftmost open pane. The open views MUST be remembered between visits (local storage) and written to the address as `?view=` and their names, such as `?view=wiki,graph`, so a shared link opens as it was seen. Switching views MUST NOT lose keyboard focus: the toggles stay where they are, and when the focused element goes away with its pane, focus MUST move to the toggle of the view just switched. On a phone one view MUST show at a time (`LA-PLT-UC08-R02`).

title: Every gap between panes resizes them, and any pane can be shown alone
statement: Every gap between two open panes MUST be a handle that resizes the two panes beside it. Each pane MUST have a full screen button, and Ctrl+3 MUST show only the focused pane (the leftmost, when focus is in none), like VS Code's maximize editor group; Ctrl+3 again, Escape or the same button MUST return to the panes, with focus back on the button.

title: Both panes follow one focus, and Back and Forward move both
statement: Clicking a record in the graph MUST change the address, so the wiki pane and the side bar follow; following a link in the wiki MUST re-center the graph. Back and Forward MUST move both panes. The graph's depth, filters, open groups and trace mode MUST survive moving between pages and switching views.

title: A group has a simple wiki page
statement: A group's wiki page MUST show its parent (as a link), its kind (with the kind's description), and its members as a list, each with its coverage marks and problem badge.

title: Product and domain pages have the same views
statement: A product's and a domain's overview pages MUST offer the Wiki and Graph views, and a domain's the Model view too; their graph MUST be centered on the product or the domain.

title: Every list that can grow stays at ten rows, in every view
statement: Every list that can grow, including the side bar's lists (raw links, a product's or domain's children, problems, what the graph connects, the files a trace reaches, the outline's rows) and a group page's members, MUST use the long list: ten rows, then a scroll inside with a search box and a count.

title: The nav collapses to a rail, and is a full-screen sheet on a narrow screen
statement: A toggle MUST collapse the nav to a narrow rail of icons (the logo, Quick find, the spaces, Checks), each with a tooltip and an accessible name, and expand it again; the state MUST be remembered. Under about 900 px wide the nav MUST become a full-screen sheet opened from the menu button in the top bar, with focus moved into it and kept inside it, and closed by Escape, its close button or choosing a page, with focus returned to the menu button.

title: The nav folds by section and shows where you are
statement: The Tools section, and each domain and folder of the current space, MUST each fold and unfold with a chevron button carrying `aria-expanded`; the section holding the current page MUST open itself. The current space MUST have no heading of its own, since the rail names it: its first row is its overview. The current page MUST be marked clearly with `aria-current="page"` and scrolled into view. Icons MUST be inline line icons; counts MUST be quiet badges, with errors red and warnings amber on Checks; long names MUST be cut short with the full name as a tooltip; items MUST be at least 32 px high. A footer MUST say where the specs come from (the record format is a command and a link in the shortcuts sheet, as `LA-AUT-UC14-R06` says).

title: Quick find jumps to anything by ID or title
statement: A search field at the top of the nav MUST find any record, domain or product by ID or title, best matches first (exact ID, ID prefix, title), and MUST let the person move through the results with the arrow keys and open one with Enter.

title: The side bar folds away
statement: A record, group, product or domain page MUST have three columns: the nav, the main view and the side bar, with the views Details, Outline and History (`LA-EXP-UC12`). One side bar MUST serve the page in every view, and show nothing the main view already shows beside it (`LA-EXP-DR55`). It MUST fold away with a toggle in the page bar and a shortcut, remember that per view mode and per tab (`LA-EXP-UC12-R02`), give its space to the main view, and on a narrow screen open as a bottom sheet that takes focus, keeps it inside, and closes with Escape (`LA-PLT-UC08-R04`).

title: Wiki pages and the side bar open one level deep
statement: A product page MUST list its domains (and its summary and questions) but not their contents; a domain page its direct children grouped by kind (Aggregates, Use cases, Flows, Views, Endpoints, Components, Tests, Open questions, and any other kind such as capabilities, in their `position`), each row showing its count of children; a record page its fields, its text, direct children and links; a group page its members. Each row with children MUST have a disclosure button (`aria-expanded`, a chevron) and each section an Expand all / Collapse all button. What is opened MUST be remembered for the session while moving around. A search inside a section MUST reveal matching nested records by opening their row just for the match. Right arrow MUST open a row (or move into it) and Left close it (or move to its parent). The command palette MUST offer Expand all and Collapse all for the page.

title: The title above a graph or a model keeps one height
statement: When the page's title sits at the top of a graph or a model pane, it MUST keep one fixed height whatever the record, each line cut with an ellipsis and the whole title in its tooltip, so the canvas below never moves when the focus changes. In the wiki pane the title MAY wrap.

title: Grouped requirements and rules read under their group headings
statement: The wiki MUST show a record's children that name a group, such as a use case's requirements, a view's interaction requirements, a pattern's rules or a standard's rules, under their group headings: the ungrouped ones first, without a heading, then each group in the order it first appears. A use case's requirement table and a standard's rule table MUST head each group's rows with its name, and the side bar's Outline MUST list the groups.

title: A flow's page shows its steps in order as a table
statement: A flow's record page MUST show its steps, when it has any, as a table in step order with the columns Step (order and ID), What happens (the title), Uses and Carries out, each linked ID going to its record.

title: A step's description and linked titles fold under its row
statement: Each step row MUST show one level: the step and the IDs it links to. Its description and the titles and kinds of what it uses and fulfills MUST be folded under the row's disclosure, with Expand all and Collapse all for the table.

title: A step row shows its problems, and a flow without steps shows no table
statement: A step's row MUST carry a badge for its errors or warnings. A flow with no steps MUST NOT show a steps table.

title: In the graph a flow step sits under its flow
statement: In the graph a flow step MUST sit one column to the right of its flow, joined to it by the parent line, and, as for other children, MUST reach them through a group only when the flow also has children of another kind.

title: A trace shows the fulfilling step, its flow and the components it uses
statement: Trace mode for a requirement or rule MUST show each flow step that fulfills it, the flow the step belongs to, and the components the step uses, with the step between its flow and those components.

title: A flow with several paths shows a table per path
statement: When a flow's steps sit on more than one `path` (a step with no path is on the main path), its page MUST show each path as its own table, headed by the path's name, the main path first and then the others by name, each in its own step order, never interleaved by `order` across paths.

title: A technical flow's page shows its steps, with their components and what they satisfy
statement: A technical flow's page MUST show its steps as a flow's page does, a table per path in order, with the columns Step, What happens, Component and Satisfies, and each step's transaction, locks and statements folded under its row with its description.

title: A trace shows a satisfying technical step, its technical flow and its component
statement: Trace mode for a requirement or rule MUST show each technical step that satisfies it, the technical flow it belongs to, and the component it uses, with the step just before that component.

title: The rail lists each product as a space
statement: The nav MUST have a rail about 56 px wide at its far left with one square icon per product in the products' ID order, and no item above every product. Each item MUST name itself in a tooltip.

title: The current space is marked
statement: The rail MUST mark the current space with an accent bar and `aria-current`.

title: The nav lists only the current space's things
statement: The nav MUST list the current space's product page, its domains, each folding into its Define and Design folders as the schema's folders place them (with the capabilities in order under Define › Capabilities), and its groups (the product's other kinds of children), and MUST NOT list another product's domains.

title: Choosing a space opens the last page visited in it
statement: Choosing a space MUST open the last page visited in that space during the session, or its product page when there is none.

title: Alt and a number switch spaces
statement: Alt+1 to Alt+9 (⌥1 to ⌥9 on a Mac) MUST switch to the first nine spaces in rail order, and the command palette MUST offer a "Switch to <product>" command for each, with its keys. Every other shortcut MUST keep working.

title: Quick find searches the current space only
statement: Quick find MUST search only the current space's records (and the record format's kinds and checks), as one list for the arrow keys, and MUST NOT list anything of another product: switching product is the rail's job.

title: Each space has its own Checks page
statement: Each space MUST have its own Checks page, inside the space at its product's ID (`/<product-id>/checks`), opened from the nav's Tools and by the Checks shortcuts; there MUST be no Checks page for every product at once.

title: The rail stays in the nav sheet on a narrow screen
statement: On a narrow screen the rail MUST stay visible inside the nav sheet.

title: No view in a space shows another product
statement: Inside a space the side bar (Details, Outline, History), the graph and its trail and minimap, the Model view, hover cards, the reference's records and its "where the X are" links, saved tabs and the space's last page MUST show only that product, and the desktop Dock badge MUST count only its problems and the workspace's. A link into another product MUST NOT be drawn or listed, and another product's ID named in a text field MUST show as plain text, not as a link.

title: The products page is the space chooser
statement: The products page (`/`), the rail's home and the only page of the specs outside every space, MUST list each product with its name and domain count, and nothing from inside the products: no problems and no coverage.

title: The nav reads like stage folders
statement: Under the current space, the nav MUST list the product page; then Shared, only when the product has patterns, holding them; then each domain, which unfolds into Define (Domain model, Use cases) and Design (Interaction design, Technical specification, Test plan), then its open questions.

title: Stages and folders fold one level at a time, with counts
statement: Every domain, stage and folder MUST be a foldable row showing one level when opened; only the level under the space MUST show by default. Each stage and folder MUST show its count of records, and one with no records MUST NOT be listed.

title: The current page's branch opens itself
statement: Opening a page from the nav, or on the nav's first draw (a load, a reload, the nav expanded or opened as a drawer), MUST open the nav rows that hold it: a domain page its domain; a record page its domain, stage and folder (or Shared); a group page the folder of its kind. A page opened anywhere else (a link in the page, the graph, Back, quick find) MUST leave the nav's rows where they are (`LA-PLT-UC09-R02`): the closed row that holds the page is marked instead, and opening that row opens the branch down to the page.

title: Use cases lists capabilities, then use cases outside any
statement: The Use cases folder MUST list the domain's capabilities in their order, then the use cases outside any capability; a capability's own use cases stay under it. A capability's flows and tests MUST be listed in Interaction design and Test plan.

title: The domain page and group pages use the same folders as headings
statement: The domain page MUST head its records with the same stages and folders as the nav (Define: Domain model, Use cases; Design: Interaction design, Technical specification, Test plan), listing a folder's records directly or under one heading per kind when it holds several, and keeping its one-level-deep folding. A group page MUST name the stage and folder of its kind, such as Design › Interaction design.

title: Technical specification lists layers in order, each with its components
statement: A domain's Technical specification MUST list its layers in their order, each holding its components, then the components sitting directly in the domain under "Components outside any layer". A domain with no layers MUST list its components directly, as before.

title: Test plan groups tests by family and by what they prove
statement: A domain's Test plan MUST place each test in one group, by its family first: Acceptance tests (it sits under a capability or proves a UC requirement), grouped by capability in order with use cases outside any capability last, then by the first use case it proves in ID order, a capability's test proving no UC requirement sitting in the capability itself; Domain rule tests; Pattern tests, grouped by pattern; Interaction tests; UI tests (`test_type` `ui`, or proving an interaction requirement at a view); Design checks (`test_type` `design`, or only `supports` links); Engineering checks (everything else). The groups MUST be computed from the tests' parents, types and links, not stored, and an empty group MUST NOT be shown.

title: Layers and test groups fold in the nav, with counts
statement: In the side nav, layers and test groups MUST be foldable rows with their counts, one level shown by default, and the current page's branch MUST open itself through its layer or its test groups. A layer's row MUST link to the layer's page; a test group's row MUST only fold. What is folded MUST last for the session.

title: The domain page and group pages head the same groups
statement: The domain page MUST head Technical specification's layers (each linking to its page) and Test plan's groups with the same names and order as the nav, keeping its one-level-deep folding of records and its filter. A group page of tests MUST read them in the same groups.

title: A layer's page lists its components
statement: A layer's record page MUST show it as a capability's is shown: its text, its fields and its components as its children, each with its own children folded.

title: The graph reaches components and tests through the same groups
statement: In the graph a domain with layers MUST reach its components through Layers, then a layer, which points straight at its components, as a capability points straight at its use cases. A parent's Tests folder MUST hold the test plan's groups from the same folder model, each a group node that opens like the others; when only one group has tests, they MUST hang directly under the Tests folder. Depth 1 MUST still show the parent and children only, and the columns MUST read left to right.

title: The graph trail names what was visited
statement: The graph's trail of visited records MUST show a record as its title with its ID in parentheses, such as "Exploring (LA-EXP)", and a group by its name alone, without a count, such as "Use cases", naming its parent in its tooltip and accessible name. A long name MUST be cut short with an ellipsis, with the full text in its tooltip, and the current item MUST stay bold.

title: Sub-layers nest, and rules under an entity sit under it
statement: A layer inside another layer MUST show as a group within that layer's group, in its order, in the nav and on the domain page alike, and a component's branch MUST open through each layer above it. A domain rule under an entity MUST be listed under that entity wherever the entity's children are, on the domain and aggregate pages, and its nav branch MUST open to the aggregate holding it.

title: A plain open uses the preview tab, or activates the page's open tab
statement: Opening a page by a plain click (a record link, a graph node or box, the nav, quick find, or Back and Forward) MUST open it in the preview tab, whose title is italic, replacing that tab's page in place; with no preview tab, a new one MUST open after the active tab. A page already open in a tab MUST activate that tab instead, as it was. Cmd- or Ctrl-click and middle-click on a link MUST still open a new browser tab.

title: A tab is kept by double-click, the Keep open command or switching its views
statement: The preview tab MUST become a lasting tab, which the next plain open no longer replaces, when the reader double-clicks it, runs the "Keep the tab open" command (`keepTab`: Ctrl+K then Enter on a Mac, as in VS Code, and Alt+K then Enter elsewhere, where Ctrl+K is quick open), or opens or closes one of its views.

title: A tab closes by its button, a middle-click or Alt+Shift+W
statement: Each tab MUST have a close button, shown on hover, on focus and on the active tab. Middle-clicking a tab MUST close it, and Alt+Shift+W (`closeTab`) MUST close the active tab; never Ctrl+W, which toggles the Wiki view on a Mac and closes the browser tab elsewhere. Closing the active tab MUST activate its neighbor to the right, or else to the left, and move the address there.

title: Ctrl+Tab cycles the tabs, and the strip works as a tab list
statement: Ctrl+Tab (`nextTab`) and Ctrl+Shift+Tab (`previousTab`) MUST activate the next and previous tab in tab order, wrapping at the ends, and with the other tab commands MUST be listed in the shortcuts sheet and the palette, their keys in tooltips and `aria-keyshortcuts`. The strip MUST be a `tablist` of `tab` elements with `aria-selected`, only the active tab in the Tab order; with a tab focused, the arrow keys, Home and End MUST move between tabs, Enter or Space MUST activate the focused one and Delete MUST close it.

title: Each tab keeps its own views, pane sizes, wiki scroll and graph settings
statement: Each tab MUST keep its own open views, pane sizes, wiki scroll position and graph settings (depth, trace, filters, open groups), and activating it MUST bring them back. A new tab MUST start from the active tab's views, sizes and settings, at the top of the page; a link that names views opens a new tab in those.

title: Tabs are kept per space for the session and come back on reload
statement: The open tabs, their order, which one is the preview and which is active, and each tab's state MUST be kept per space for the browser session; switching spaces MUST swap the tab set for that space's own. Reloading MUST bring back the same tabs, the same active tab and each tab's views. A saved tab or space's last page that is not a page's address MUST be dropped.

title: The tab strip leads the page bar, each tab with ID and title
statement: The tab strip MUST sit at the left of the page bar above the panes, apart from the panes' own headers, which name their views. Each tab MUST show its record's ID in mono and its title, cut short with an ellipsis, with both in full in its tooltip; a group's tab MUST show its label ("Use cases (7)"). Tabs that do not fit MUST scroll sideways by wheel or trackpad, and the active tab MUST scroll into view; the page bar keeps its height. On a phone the tabs MUST fold into an "Open pages" button in the page bar that opens them as a sheet (`LA-PLT-UC08-R05`).

title: Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch record tabs in the desktop app
statement: View › Tabs MUST offer Show Next Tab, Show Previous Tab, Keep Tab Open and Close Tab, running `nextTab`, `previousTab`, `keepTab` and `closeTab` by command ID. Show Next Tab and Show Previous Tab MUST own Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab as their accelerators, since a web page never receives those keys; the other two MUST take no key from the app.

title: The Model view is offered on domain, aggregate and entity pages only
statement: A domain, aggregate or entity page MUST offer a Model view, a pane toggled like Wiki and Graph and sitting after them. Any other page MUST NOT offer it, and an address that names it there MUST show the page's other named views.

title: A domain's ERD draws its aggregates and how their entities refer to each other
statement: On a domain the Model view MUST draw one box per aggregate, with its title, its root entity's name and its count of entities, and one line for each aggregate pair and direction that a `refers_to` link between their entities joins, with a crow's foot at the referring end and one at the other (many to one). An aggregate whose entities refer to no other aggregate MUST show its `relates_to` links instead, drawn dashed. A referenced aggregate in another domain MUST appear gray, labeled with its domain in parentheses.

title: An aggregate's ERD draws its entities with their fields and relationships
statement: On an aggregate the Model view MUST draw one box per entity, with its title, a root mark on the root, and each field's name and kind of value, and a line for each `has_one` (one to one), `has_many` (one to many) and `refers_to` (many to one) link its entities hold, with those crow's-foot ends. An entity it refers to in another aggregate of the domain MUST be labeled with that aggregate in parentheses, and one in another domain MUST appear gray, labeled "(Domain · Aggregate)".

title: An entity's ERD is its aggregate's, with the entity picked out
statement: On an entity the Model view MUST draw its aggregate's ERD with the entity highlighted.

title: Boxes lead to their pages, and a key explains the diagram
statement: Clicking a box, or pressing Enter on it, MUST go to its page, keeping the open views, and a box MUST show a hover state; the highlighted entity on its own page leads nowhere. A key under the diagram MUST explain the colors, with 🟦 for the current domain and ⬜ for another, and the line ends.

title: The ERD shows the next ring out, faded, and frames what is in focus
statement: On an aggregate's ERD, the entities that its referenced entities refer to MUST appear one ring out, faded and out of focus, with their lines faded. On a domain's ERD, the aggregates of other domains MUST be faded context too. The camera MUST frame the boxes in focus only, and edge hints MUST count the faded boxes past each edge (see LA-EXP-DR48).

title: An aggregate's ERD shows the domain events it raises and who reacts to them
statement: On an aggregate's ERD, each of its domain events MUST appear as a flag, notched on the right, beside its entities, in the spark colors, naming the event and how many fields it carries. Where the event has `raised_by`, a short line MUST run to it from the entity that raises it; an event with none stands on its own. Each aggregate that reacts to the event, from this domain or another, MUST appear as faded context (another domain's gray and named in parentheses) at the end of a dashed "reacts to" line from the event. An event's page MUST offer the Model view, drawing its aggregate's ERD with its pill picked out.

title: A domain's ERD shows which aggregates react to which aggregates' events
statement: On a domain's ERD, a dashed "reacts to" line MUST run from an aggregate that raises an event to each aggregate that reacts to it, with an arrow at the reacting end, so the reader sees cause and effect: one line per aggregate pair and event (see LA-EXP-DR51). Hovering a line MUST show the event's name as its label; by touch the name always shows. An aggregate of another domain on either end is gray, faded context.

title: The key explains the event flag and its lines
statement: When an ERD draws domain events or "reacts to" lines, its key MUST explain the event flag, the line from the entity that raises an event and the dashed "reacts to" line, in the relations' own labels from the meta-model, without changing the key's height.

title: One side bar with three views, chosen from a switcher at its top
statement: The page's last column MUST be one side bar with a switcher at its top of three icon buttons, Details, Outline and History, each with `aria-pressed` and a tooltip, in a group labeled "Side bar views". The view shown MUST have a heading naming it and be the region the switcher's buttons control. Switching MUST keep keyboard focus on the button pressed and announce the view. The side bar keeps its width handle, its toggle in the page bar and its shortcut (`LA-EXP-UC05-R11`).

title: The side bar keeps its open state and view per view mode and per tab
