statement: The side bar's view mode MUST be the Wiki view when only the wiki is open, and otherwise the Graph or Model view open beside it. Each mode MUST keep whether the side bar is open and which view it shows, per tab (`LA-EXP-UC10`) across a reload, and as last used for a space's first tab. Until the Reader chooses, it MUST be closed in the Wiki view and open on Details in the Graph and Model views. On a phone it MUST stay a bottom sheet (`LA-PLT-UC08-R04`) with the same three views.

title: Details follows the pointer and the selection, and repeats nothing the page shows
statement: In the Graph and Model views Details MUST show the node under the pointer or keyboard focus (the graph's spotlight), else the one selected by a tap, else the page's record: its kind, title and ID, its columns, data file and parent, its problems, and a compact Traceability in the relations' labels (`LA-EXP-V03-R07`), with Open for any other record and, in the desktop app, Reveal and Open in editor. In the Graph view it also lists what the graph connects to the center. In the Wiki view Details MUST show a record row that has focus or was right-clicked the same way, and otherwise only what the page leaves out: the data file and line, the columns of its row and the raw links both ways, plus a product's or domain's parent, children and problems, which its overview does not list.

title: Outline lists what the main view holds, as rows to jump to
statement: In the Wiki view Outline MUST list the page's sections and headings (Traceability and its groups, children, problems, the headings in its text) in page order and indented by level; a click MUST scroll the wiki to that heading, and the section in view MUST be marked (`aria-current="location"`) as the wiki scrolls. In the Graph view it MUST list the records the camera frames, grouped by level from left to right; in the Model view the diagram's boxes, those in focus first. Every list MUST be rows that are clickable anywhere (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R05`) and searchable past ten rows (`LA-EXP-UC05-R07`).

title: History lists the commits that changed the record's rows, with what each changed
statement: History MUST list the commits that changed the selected record's rows (or the page's record's) in the data files, newest first, each with its date, author, subject and short hash, twenty at a time with "Load more". Changes in the working tree not committed yet MUST come first, labeled "Not committed". Each commit MUST show what it changed in the record's rows, the fields before and after, marked with the theme's tokens. When the product folder is not a git repository, or git is missing, it MUST say so calmly, as a hint, not an error. A group has no rows of its own, and says so.

title: Switching the side bar's view or what it describes moves nothing outside it
statement: Switching between Details, Outline and History, and Details following the pointer or the selection, MUST change only the side bar's content: the nav, the panes, their bars and titles, the canvas, the side bar's own box and its switcher MUST hold still (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R08`). A hover MUST redraw only the side bar, never the canvas.

title: An API's page lists its endpoints and the requirements they share
statement: An API's page MUST list its endpoints, each with its method and route, and then its shared requirements, the interaction requirements under the API, each in its own section with its count, in place of the plain list of children.

title: An integration's page lists its exchanges and names its system
statement: An integration's page MUST list its exchanges, the interaction requirements under it, in a section with its count, saying which outside system they are with when the integration names one.

title: APIs and integrations sit in Interaction design, and technical flows in Technical specification
statement: The nav, the domain page and the graph MUST place an API and an integration in the Interaction design folder, and a technical flow in Technical specification, in the group of the layer it sits in, from each kind's folder in the meta-model.

title: Every record page has Edit, which opens its form in place
statement: Every record's page MUST offer Edit, Add and Remove as buttons in its record actions. Edit MUST open the record's form in place of the page's content, holding its columns, its parent, its links and its part rows as they are; Save MUST send every change as one write, and Cancel MUST leave the record as it was.

title: Inputs follow the schema, and pickers offer only valid targets
statement: Each input MUST take the type of its column (`LA-EXP-DR66`), an enum as a select of its values; the parent and each link MUST be picked from the records they may name, in the same product, and the form MUST say before it writes when a required input is empty or a value is not of its type.

title: A child is added from its parent's page
statement: Add MUST open an empty form for a record of a kind that may sit under the page's record (a choice of kind when several may), with that record as its parent and the next free ID suggested, and MUST add it in one write.

title: Remove asks first, naming what still references the record
statement: Remove MUST ask first, listing what still references the record (its children, the links into it, other records' rows that name it); while anything does, it MUST say the removal will be refused until those go. Confirming MUST send one write that removes the record with its part rows and the links it starts.

title: A refusal shows inline with its reasons
statement: A write the store refuses MUST show its reasons at the top of the form or question and beside the input each came from (`LA-EXP-DR67`), in the store's own words without a file and line, and the person MUST be able to fix the input and save again.

title: Editing works from the keyboard and a screen reader
statement: The record actions, the form and the remove question MUST work from the keyboard alone, as the rest of the app does: every input labeled, a required input marked as required, an input with a problem marked invalid and described by its message, focus taken to the form's first input when it opens and back to its action when it closes, and a change announced. They MUST pass the accessibility suite (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R10`) with no finding.

title: loadWorkspace returns the Workspace contract
statement: `loadWorkspace(root)` MUST return a `Workspace` as defined in `lathe/src/types.ts`. Fields MAY be added to that contract but MUST NOT be renamed or removed.

title: Each record's product and domain come from its parents
statement: The engine MUST give each record its `product` and `domain` from its parent columns, through the store's `record_scope` view. Data the store refuses, such as a cycle of parents, MUST make the load end with one `data-refused` error per refusal, naming the file, line and rule, and no records, rather than loop or load in part.

title: Loading is fast enough to reload live
statement: `loadWorkspace(root)` MUST load Lathe's own spec in under 2 s, and load it again after one row changes in under 500 ms (`LA-PLT-DR02`), so the app and an agent's script can reload on every write. It MAY take `timings` in its options, which it fills with how long each phase took (open, files, checks, coverage, total).

title: Init writes a config and a first product record
statement: `lathe init --name <name> --prefix <prefix>` MUST write `lathe.config.json` when the repo has none, and MUST add the product record with that ID and title to `data/product.jsonl` through the store. It MUST refuse a prefix that is not a valid ID and MUST NOT overwrite an existing product record.

title: The product's config names its data folder
statement: Every command MUST read the data folder from the `data` key of the product's `lathe.config.json`, defaulting to `data`, and MUST NOT read records from any other folder. A setting the config does not define MUST be refused with an error that names it.

title: A product adds its own kinds without forking Lathe
statement: A product's own kinds and relations MUST be `product_kind`, `product_kind_field` and `product_relation` rows in its own data, which add tables to the schema for that product only. They MUST NOT widen one of Lathe's kinds; that takes a migration.

title: Serve needs no build tools in the product repo
statement: `lathe serve` MUST serve the web app and its API for the product repo from the installed package alone, and open pages MUST reload when the product's data files change.

title: Each clone sets up the merge driver for the data files
statement: A product repo's `.gitattributes` MUST name its data files for the `lathe-data` merge driver (`**/data/*.jsonl merge=lathe-data`), and the README MUST say how each clone sets it up once with `git config merge.lathe-data.name` and `git config merge.lathe-data.driver "npx lathe merge-data %O %A %B %P"`, so two branches' new rows merge row by row instead of clashing line by line.

title: Pages reload when the data files or Lathe's checks change
statement: When a file in the product's data folder, or one of Lathe's own check rows or migrations, changes, the server SHOULD send `spec:changed`, and the open page SHOULD then load the data again without a manual refresh, staying at the same address.

title: One keymap table drives the keys, the palette and the sheet
statement: Every keyboard command MUST be one row in one table (command id, title, group, default keys, where it applies), and the key handlers, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST all be drawn from it, so nothing is listed twice. "Mod" MUST mean Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere, in matching and in what the app shows (⌘⇧P on a Mac, Ctrl+Shift+P elsewhere).

title: The default shortcuts follow VS Code
statement: The defaults MUST be: Cmd/Ctrl+P and Cmd/Ctrl+K quick open; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P the command palette; Cmd/Ctrl+B the nav; Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+B the side bar; Ctrl+W (Alt+W off a Mac) or Ctrl+1, Ctrl+G (Alt+G) or Ctrl+2, and Ctrl+M (Alt+M) or Ctrl+4 the Wiki, Graph and Model views on and off; Ctrl+3 the focused pane alone (full screen) and back, with Escape to leave it; Ctrl+- and Ctrl+Shift+- back and forward (Alt+Left and Alt+Right left to the browser); F12 open the focused link's record; Shift+F12 the incoming links in the side bar; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M Checks; F8 and Shift+F8 the next and previous problem on the page; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E focus the nav; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+I or Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+I focus the side bar; `/` the nearest search box; `?` and Cmd/Ctrl+/ the shortcuts sheet; in the graph `+` and `-` depth, `t` trace mode, `v` the next of the Tree, Nested and Voronoi layouts, `.` fit, with the arrow keys and Enter as before; and `g` then `c`, `f` or `h` for Checks, the format and home, with a small hint while the second key is awaited.

title: Shortcuts never get in the way of typing or of the browser
statement: Single-key shortcuts MUST NOT fire while typing; the app MUST call preventDefault only for keys it handles (so Cmd/Ctrl+P never opens the print dialog, and unhandled keys reach the browser); and no binding MUST take a browser essential.

title: A command palette and a shortcuts sheet, both searchable
statement: The command palette MUST list every command that applies on the current page with its shortcut, filter as the person types, and run the chosen one with Enter. The shortcuts sheet MUST list every shortcut grouped as Navigate, View, Graph and Lists, with a search box. Both MUST be dialogs that take focus, keep Tab inside, close with Escape and give focus back.

title: A person can change the bindings
statement: The app MUST read optional overrides from local storage (`lathe:keybindings`, a JSON map of command id to a binding or a list of bindings), ignore unknown commands and bad values, and say how in the shortcuts sheet, with each command's id shown.

title: Every command works without a mouse and is announced
statement: Every command MUST be reachable from the keyboard, and a command that changes the view (a view switch, a panel shown or hidden, full screen, the next problem) MUST be announced to screen readers through a polite live region.

title: A command's keys suit the platform
statement: A command MAY have other keys off a Mac. On a Mac, Ctrl means the Control key, so Ctrl+W leaves Cmd+W to the browser; elsewhere Ctrl+W closes the tab and Ctrl+G finds the next match, so the view toggles take Alt+W, Alt+G and Alt+M there. A binding that is reserved for the browser on the current platform MUST never be offered, even through an override, and tooltips, `aria-keyshortcuts`, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST show the keys for the current platform.

title: A tooltip shows the control and its keys
statement: Every icon button and control that has a shortcut MUST show it in its tooltip as its name then its keys ("Show or hide the navigation ⌘B", or "Ctrl+B" off a Mac), after a short hover delay and at once on keyboard focus.

title: Menus and the palette show each command's keys at the right
statement: The command palette, and any menu, MUST show each command's first shortcut right-aligned on its row in `<kbd>` styling; a command without one shows none.

title: A control with a shortcut has aria-keyshortcuts
statement: Every control with a shortcut MUST carry `aria-keyshortcuts` with its keys.

title: The shortcuts sheet matches the hints
statement: The shortcuts sheet (`?`) MUST list the same keys the hints show, with one "Switch to <product>" row per product that has a key.

title: A gap between panels resizes them by drag or keyboard
statement: Each gap between two panels MUST resize them when dragged, and when focused MUST step with the arrow keys (bigger steps with Shift) and jump to the limits with Home and End, the arrow toward a panel growing it. Each size MUST stay within its limits: the navigation 256 to 560 px, the side bar 260 to 640 px, and each pane 20 to 80 percent of the two panes beside a gap, and never narrower than 220 px.

title: Sizes are remembered, and double-click resets one
statement: Each panel's size MUST be remembered across visits (each pane's as a fraction of the panes' width, so it holds whichever panes are open), a remembered size outside its limits MUST fall back to the default, and double-clicking a gap MUST reset its size to the default (navigation 304 px, side bar 340 px), or for a gap between two panes share their space evenly.

title: Dragging the navigation or the side bar small folds it
statement: Dragging the navigation below 180 px MUST fold it to its rail, and dragging the side bar below 160 px MUST hide it; dragging the rail's gap out again MUST unfold the navigation. On a narrow screen there MUST be no gaps to drag: the navigation and the side bar are sheets.

title: The Color theme command previews each theme and keeps or puts back
statement: The "Color theme" command (`chooseTheme`, g then t) MUST open a quick pick of every theme. Arrowing to a theme MUST show it on the whole app at once, without keeping it; Enter or a click MUST keep it, and Escape or a click outside MUST put back the theme shown before.

title: Light, dark or system is chosen in the app
statement: Every theme MUST show its light or dark set by the person's choice of System (the default, following `prefers-color-scheme`), Light or Dark. The choice MUST be made by the "Light, dark or system" command (`chooseColorMode`), which previews like the theme picker, and on the Appearance page.

title: The Appearance page lists the themes with previews
statement: `/settings/appearance` MUST list every theme, built in and the reader's own, each with a small preview of the app in its colors and fonts, the one in use marked, and buttons to use it, to duplicate and edit it (built in) or edit it (his own), and to export it. The page MUST be linked from the nav's footer and reachable from the command palette ("Open Appearance settings").

title: A copy of a theme can be edited, renamed, reset and deleted
statement: "Duplicate and edit" MUST make a copy and open it in an editor with: color pickers grouped by purpose (surfaces, text, borders, accent, signals, graph and depth), the light and dark sets side by side; fonts for headings, text and code from a short safe list or a custom font stack; text size, density (comfortable or compact), panel corner radius, gap between panels, and motion (follow the system or always reduced). The theme being edited MUST be the one in use, so the app around the editor is its live preview, beside small light and dark previews. The editor MUST rename the theme, reset it to the built-in it was copied from, and delete it after asking.

title: Hard-to-read colors are flagged while editing
statement: While editing, each text or control color whose contrast on what it is drawn on falls below WCAG AA (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and controls) MUST show a warning beside its swatch, with the ratio, the background and the ratio it needs, for the mode it fails in.

title: Themes are kept per person and travel as files
statement: The reader's own themes, the chosen theme and the mode MUST be kept per person (in the browser's local storage, behind a store the desktop app can replace), and MUST survive a reload. Any theme MUST export as a small, versioned JSON file, and such a file MUST import as a new theme of his own.

title: A theme applies at once and before first paint
statement: Choosing a theme or a mode MUST apply at once, without a reload. On load, the chosen theme and mode MUST be on the page before the first paint, so it never flashes another theme.

title: Below 900 px wide the app has a compact top bar and fits the screen
statement: Below 900 px wide the app MUST take its phone layout. Its top bar MUST hold the menu button, the page's title on one line (cut with an ellipsis) under a link one step up (to the record's parent, a domain's product, or all products, keeping the view in front), and a quick find button. The layout MUST fill the screen's dynamic height (`100dvh`), keep its bars and sheets clear of the safe areas (`env(safe-area-inset-*)`, with `viewport-fit=cover`), and no page MUST scroll sideways at 320 px wide.

title: A phone shows one view at a time, switched from the page bar
statement: On a phone a record, group, product or domain page MUST show one view at a time, full width, with no pane headers and no resize handles: the first of the views the address names. The page bar MUST sit under the top bar, compact: the Open pages button, the View switch (Wiki, Graph and Model where offered, one pressed) and the side bar toggle. Switching MUST show that view alone, name it in the address (`?view=graph`) and keep it in the tab, and MUST leave the views remembered for a wide screen alone.

title: The nav is a full-screen sheet with the same rows, sized for a thumb
statement: On a phone the nav MUST open from the top bar's menu button as a full-screen sheet that slides in from the left, keeps the space rail, takes focus to its quick find, keeps Tab inside it, and closes by Escape, its close button or choosing a page, giving focus back to the menu button. Its rows MUST be the wide screen's rows (`LA-EXP-DR41`), at least 44 px tall on a touch screen, with the fold chevrons as large targets.

title: The side bar is a bottom sheet at half or full height
statement: On a phone the side bar MUST open from the page bar as a bottom sheet with a grab handle, at half the screen's height. Dragging the handle up or tapping it MUST take it to full height; dragging it down MUST take it back to half, or close it from half; a flick MUST count as a long drag. Escape, a tap on the dimmed page above it or its close button MUST close it. It MUST take focus as it opens, keep Tab inside it, and give focus back to its toggle when it closes.

title: The open pages are a sheet
statement: On a phone the tabs MUST fold into an Open pages button in the page bar that shows how many are open and opens them as a bottom sheet: one row per tab with its ID and title, the active one marked, the preview's title in italics with a Keep button, and a close button on every row. Choosing a row MUST go to that page and close the sheet.

title: Quick find and the command palette fill the screen
statement: On a phone quick find MUST open from the top bar (and from its shortcut) as a full-screen sheet: the search box at the top with a Close button, the results as a list under it, more of them than in the dropdown. Choosing a result MUST go there and close the sheet; Escape or Close MUST close it and give focus back. The command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST fill the screen too.

title: The graph and the ERD pan, pinch and take taps
statement: The graph and the ERD MUST pan with a finger and zoom with a pinch. On a touch screen a first tap on a node MUST select it: the node is outlined and a card at the bottom of the canvas shows its kind and name with an Open chip; a second tap on it, or the chip, MUST open it; a tap on the empty canvas MUST let it go. A click with a mouse MUST still open a node at once. A long press does nothing of its own: the tap's card is the preview.

title: Pages are readable on a phone
statement: On a phone body text MUST be at least 16 px, and every text box MUST be 16 px so the phone does not zoom in on focus. Long IDs MUST wrap rather than widen the page; wide tables and code blocks MUST scroll sideways inside their own box; long lists MUST keep their ten rows with a search (`LA-TRC-DR35`). A record row MUST stack: its ID on a line of its own, its title under it at the row's full width, and its meta (counts, tags, marks) below, so a title is never squeezed beside an ID.

title: The browser chrome follows the theme, and sheets move only when motion is welcome
statement: The page MUST carry a `theme-color` meta that follows the theme's sheet color, in light and dark and for any theme chosen. Sheets MUST slide in with the shared motion tokens and MUST appear at once when the system asks for reduced motion (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R04`).

title: A tablet in landscape keeps the workbench, sized for touch
statement: The screen's width MUST decide the layout and the pointer the size of targets: at 900 px and wider, a tablet MUST keep the workbench (nav, panes, side bar), with every target at least 44 × 44 px on a touch screen (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07`); below 900 px, a tablet in portrait MUST take the phone layout.

title: The first load shifts nothing
statement: When a product, domain or record page first loads, nothing already drawn MAY move: content that arrives late (the specs, the fonts) MUST take room kept for it or appear without pushing what is drawn. The nav draws its lists once the specs have arrived; the fonts are the app's own, preloaded, and a font that is not there in time is not swapped in later.

title: Moving between records keeps the frame still
statement: Moving to another record through the nav, a link, a graph click, Back or quick find MUST keep the nav, the pane bars and the side bar where they were, and MUST draw the new page at its place from its first frame: a new page at the top, and a page reached by Back or Forward where it was scrolled. The nav's rows, the View toggles and the tabs' close buttons MUST NOT move: a View toggle the page does not offer keeps its slot, dimmed, and every tab has one width.

title: Opening, closing and maximizing panes moves only the panes
statement: Opening or closing the Wiki, Graph or Model pane, the side bar, and full screen (Ctrl+3) MUST change only the panes' widths: the nav stays, a pane that stays open is not drawn anew, and a canvas that opens appears already fitted.

title: Folding moves only what is below the row
statement: Opening or closing a row, and Expand all or Collapse all, MUST move only what is below the row or the list; the row itself, the lists above it and the page title stay, and nothing jumps and then corrects.

title: Resizing follows the pointer
statement: Dragging a gap MUST resize what sits beside it with the pointer and never jump back to a size it left; folding a panel by drag moves nothing on the far side of the page.

title: The graph and the Model view keep their canvas still
statement: Re-centering the graph at any depth, changing the depth, and moving between a domain's, an aggregate's and an entity's ERD MUST keep the pane title, the header and the canvas at one size and place; only the boxes and the camera move, on the shared motion.

title: A live reload keeps what is in view
statement: When the specs reload while the Reader is scrolled part-way down, what was at the top of the view MUST stay there, and the graph MUST NOT be drawn anew.

title: Overlays are placed before they show
statement: A tooltip, quick find, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST be placed before they show and stay where they showed; typing in their search box filters the list under it without moving the box.

title: Switching theme moves nothing
statement: Switching the theme MUST change colors only: no box moves or changes size.

title: The mobile sheets move nothing behind them
statement: At phone width (375 px), opening and closing the nav and side bar sheets MUST NOT move the page behind them.

title: Moving around answers within the performance budgets
statement: Opening a record page, switching views and re-centering the graph MUST answer within the app's performance budgets (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11`): the page is interactive within 1.5 s, a view switch takes under 100 ms of main-thread work, and a re-center at depth 3 glides at 60 Hz, with at most 3 frames over 20 ms and none of 100 ms or more, so the shared motion keeps gliding while the new picture arrives.

title: Every page passes the audit
statement: The product, domain, record and group pages, the graph and the Model view, Checks, Format and Appearance, quick find, the command palette, the shortcuts sheet, a tooltip, the side bar and the phone's sheets MUST pass axe-core's WCAG 2.2 AA rules, at 1440 px and at 375 px, in the Lathe theme and the High contrast theme, each in light and in dark.

title: Every control is reached and worked by the keyboard
statement: Tab and Shift+Tab MUST reach every control a page draws, each with a visible focus ring, and go all the way round the page and back without being held anywhere. Inside a group of controls (the tab strip, the graph's boxes, a tree's rows) the arrow keys move and Enter or Space acts. The main tasks MUST work by keyboard alone: open a record from the nav or from quick find, switch views, re-center the graph, fold and unfold a row, show, hide and focus the side bar, and pick a theme.

title: Focus lands where the Reader expects
statement: After a move to another page, focus MUST stay on the page, never fall to the body. A control that changes the page in place (a view toggle, the side bar toggle, a fold button) MUST keep focus. Re-centering the graph by keyboard MUST put focus on the box that became the center. A dialog (quick find, the palette, the shortcuts sheet, the theme picker) or a phone sheet MUST take focus when it opens, keep Tab inside it while it is open, and give focus back to the control that opened it when it closes.

title: What changes out of sight is announced
statement: When a command changes the page somewhere other than where focus is (a view opened or closed, the side bar shown or hidden, a theme chosen, every row folded), the app's one announcer (a polite live region) MUST say so in a short sentence, such as "Graph view", "Side bar hidden" or "Color theme: Midnight".

title: Open Product Folder picks a folder and opens it in its own window
statement: File › Open Product Folder… (Cmd+O, Ctrl+O elsewhere) MUST let the reader choose a folder and open it in a window of its own. A folder that is not a product MUST be refused with a message saying what is missing.

title: The window names the product and its folder
statement: The window's title MUST be the names of the products in the folder (the titles of their product records, joined by commas), then the folder, with the home folder shown as `~`. The page MUST NOT change it.

title: Open Recent lists the last 10 folders
statement: File › Open Recent MUST list the recent folders, latest first, each opening its folder, then Clear Menu; with none it MUST say No Recent Folders.

title: A window opens with the shell background, with no white flash
statement: A window MUST stay hidden until its page is ready to show, and its background MUST be the app's shell color (`--shell`) for the system's light or dark appearance, so it never flashes white.

title: Development loads the 5199 dev server when it serves the opened folder
statement: In development a window MUST load `http://localhost:5199` when that server answers for the opened folder, so app changes hot-reload exactly as in the browser.

title: Otherwise the shell starts a dev server of its own for the folder
statement: When 5199 does not answer, or answers for another folder, the shell MUST start the app's Vite dev server on a free port with `LATHE_ROOT` set to the opened folder, and load it. The dev API plugin MUST read its product folder from `LATHE_ROOT`, defaulting to Lathe's own repo, so the owner's 5199 server is unchanged.

title: A change to the main process or preload restarts Electron
statement: `npm --prefix desktop run dev` MUST rebuild the shell and restart Electron whenever a file under `desktop/src` changes. A build that fails MUST leave the running shell as it is.

title: Record changes reload the page in every mode
statement: A change to the opened product's specs MUST reload what the page shows, whether it loads `serve()`, the shell's own dev server or the 5199 server.

title: A local build is unsigned and stays on this Mac
statement: `npm --prefix desktop run pack` MUST build Lathe first, then an unsigned macOS app for this Mac's architecture in `desktop/release/`, which git ignores. It MUST NOT sign, notarize, publish or add auto-update.

title: The menus are File, Edit, View, Window and Help
statement: The shell MUST have native menus: File (Open Product Folder…, Open Recent, Close Window), Edit, View (the app commands, then Reload, Force Reload, Toggle Developer Tools, the zoom items and Toggle Full Screen), Window, and Help (Record Format, Keyboard Shortcuts), with the app menu first on a Mac.

title: A menu choice runs the app command by its ID
statement: A menu item for an app command MUST send the command's ID from the keymap (such as `viewWiki` or `toggleNav`) to the page, and the app's command system MUST run it, as if its key had been pressed.

title: The app can tell it runs in the desktop app
statement: `window.latheDesktop.isDesktop` MUST be true in the desktop app and absent in a browser, so the keymap can show desktop-only bindings later.

title: The menus take no key from the app
statement: App command items MUST carry no accelerator, so every key reaches the app's keymap, with its overrides, unchanged.

title: The window has no system title bar; the app draws its own
statement: A window MUST have no system title bar. The app MUST draw its own 38 px bar across the top of the window, on the shell color (`--shell`) with no border, so the bar and the shell are one surface, and lay the page out under it. On macOS the traffic lights MUST float over the bar's left end, centered in its height; on Windows and Linux the native window controls MUST draw over its right end. The bar MUST leave room for them. The window MUST keep its title and, on macOS, its represented folder, which the Window menu and Mission Control show.

title: Back and forward follow the app's history
statement: The bar MUST start with back and forward buttons that run the app's `goBack` and `goForward` commands. Each MUST be disabled when there is no page to go to in that direction, where the browser can tell.

title: The command center names the page and opens quick find
statement: The bar's center MUST hold a command center: a pill showing the product name and the current page's heading ("Lathe — Add an item to the basket"), centered on the window and cut short with an ellipsis when it does not fit. Clicking it MUST open quick find (`quickOpen`), and its tooltip MUST show the shortcut.

title: The layout toggles show and hide the navigation and the side bar
statement: The bar MUST end with toggle buttons for the navigation and the side bar that run `toggleNav` and `toggleSideBar`, the same commands as the menus and the keys. Each MUST say with `aria-pressed` whether its panel shows, and its tooltip MUST show the shortcut. The side bar toggle MUST be disabled on a page that has no side bar.

title: The bar drags the window, and a double-click zooms it
statement: Dragging the bar anywhere but on a control MUST move the window. Double-clicking it there MUST zoom or maximize the window, as the system's setting says. Its controls MUST take clicks and never drag.

title: The window's chrome follows the theme
statement: When the theme or the light or dark mode changes, including the system's appearance while the mode is System, the app MUST send the theme's shell and ink colors to the shell through `window.latheDesktop.setChrome`. The shell MUST then set the window's background and, on Windows and Linux, the window controls' colors.

title: In a browser there is no title bar
statement: The app MUST draw the title bar only when `window.latheDesktop` is present. In a browser the page MUST stay as it is.

title: The app icon reads at every size and in light and dark Docks
statement: The app MUST have an icon drawn on Apple's icon grid, rendered from SVG for macOS (`.icns`, 16 to 1024 px), Windows (`.ico`) and Linux (PNGs), with a bolder drawing at 16 and 32 px. A development build (`npm run dev`) MUST show the icon with a "DEV" band in the Dock.

title: The Dock menu opens a new window and lists recent folders
statement: The Dock menu MUST have New Window, which runs Open Product Folder, and every folder opened MUST be added to the system's recent documents, which macOS lists in the Dock menu.

title: About Lathe shows the versions and links to the repo and the record format
statement: About Lathe MUST open a small window with the app's, the engine's and Electron's versions and links to the repo and the record format, opened in the system browser. Check for Updates MUST NOT show until signed builds are published.

title: Settings opens the app's settings in the focused window
statement: Settings… (Cmd+,) MUST open `/settings/appearance` in the focused product window.

title: A second launch or a folder from Finder goes to the running app
statement: The app MUST run as one instance: a second launch, or a folder opened through Finder or the Dock, MUST open that folder's window in the running app, or bring it forward when it is open.

title: A window opens on the shell color with a launch view until the specs answer
statement: A new window MUST show the theme's shell color at once and a launch view (the logo and "Opening <product>…") until the page has the product's specs, with no white flash and no blank window.

title: A folder the engine cannot load gets an error page with a way on
statement: When Lathe cannot start for a folder or the engine cannot load it, the window MUST show the message with Retry, Open Another Folder and Reveal in Finder.

title: The window behaves like a native one
statement: The window MUST NOT check spelling, MUST use overlay scroll bars and native context menus (Cut, Copy and Paste on text), and MUST reopen in full screen when it was closed in full screen. In full screen on macOS the title bar MUST drop the room it keeps for the hidden traffic lights.

title: The app writes through the server, one write per request
statement: The app MUST change data only by sending one write's commands to `POST /api/write`, which MUST apply them through the store's command layer as one transaction and answer with the rows the write changed, or with the store's refusal and every reason.

title: Only the app's own pages can write
statement: The server MUST refuse a write that comes from another site's page, that is not JSON, or that holds more than its limits (1 MB, 500 commands), before the store sees it.

title: Coverage counts satisfied and proved obligations
statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give the number of obligations of each obligation kind, and how many of each are satisfied (designed) and how many are proved. Built counts are `LA-TRC-UC01-R04`; planned counts are `LA-TRC-UC02-R03`.

title: Coverage lists each gap with the missing link
statement: Coverage MUST list each obligation that is not satisfied or not proved, with its kind, saying which link (`satisfies` for design, `proves` for proof) is missing.

title: Coverage gaps are warnings, not errors
statement: An unsatisfied or unproved obligation MUST be reported as a warning, so that an honest, unfinished design still passes `lathe check`.

title: Coverage reports built separately from designed
statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give how many obligations of each kind are built: satisfied by at least one component whose `file` exists. The built count MUST never be more than the designed (satisfied) count, so a domain whose code does not exist yet shows as designed but not built.

title: Coverage counts every obligation kind
statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give one entry per kind the schema marks as an obligation (`meta_kind.obligation` full or proof), in schema order, including `interaction_requirement` and the kinds a product declares, even when the domain has none of that kind. Each entry MUST give the total and how many are designed, built, proved and planned.

title: Design and proof links are found by their role
statement: Coverage and the `unsatisfied` and `unproved` checks MUST treat a link as design or proof only by its relation's `role` (`meta_relation.role`, `design` or `proof`), so that a relation a product declares with a role counts like `satisfies` or `proves`.

title: A planned test makes an obligation planned, not proved
statement: An obligation MUST count as proved only when an automated or manual test proves it, and as planned when it is not proved but a planned test is meant to prove it. The `unproved` warning for such an obligation SHOULD say that its test is only planned.

title: The check prints one coverage line per domain and obligation kind
statement: `lathe check` MUST print one coverage line for each domain and obligation kind the domain has, with designed, built, proved and planned counts out of the total and the number of gaps; a domain with no obligations gets one line saying so.

title: Obligations and roles come from the schema's meta tables
statement: Coverage MUST read each kind's obligation from `meta_kind.obligation` (full, proof or none) and each relation's role from `meta_relation.role`, and the workspace MUST give each kind its `obligation` and `proof_only` and each relation its `role`, a product's own kinds and relations included.

title: An automated test's file names the test or every record it proves
statement: An automated test's `file` MUST name the test's own ID, or else every ID of a record the test links to with a `proof`-role relation (such as `proves`); a test with a `key` MUST instead have a file that contains the key. Each proved ID left out MUST be a `proof-not-in-file` error, and a missing key, or a missing ID of a test that proves nothing, a `test-file-missing-id` error, as LA-TRC-UC05 sets out.

title: A test's state is automated, manual or planned
statement: A test's `state` MUST be one of `automated`, `manual` and `planned`, and every test MUST give one: the store MUST refuse any other value, or none. The checks and coverage MUST read it the same way.

title: Only an automated test needs a file
statement: The store MUST refuse an automated test with no `file`. A manual or planned test MUST NOT need a `file`; if it names one, the file MUST exist (`test-file-missing`), but it MUST NOT need to mention any ID. A planned test MAY name the file it will live in before that file exists; that MUST be a warning, not an error.

title: A test may support an obligation without proving it
statement: The schema MUST have a `supports` relation from a test to each obligation kind (UC requirement, domain rule, interaction requirement and pattern rule), with no role and the labels Supports and Supported by. A `supports` link MUST NOT count as proof, and MUST NOT raise `proof-not-in-file`, `proof-still-owed` or `test-file-missing-id`.

title: A test that runs from a shared class names its key file
statement: A test MAY name in `key_file` the file that holds its key, when it runs from a shared class in another file. With a `key_file`, `proof-not-in-file` and `test-file-missing-id` MUST look for the key, or the IDs, in that file, which MUST exist and sit under the product root. The test's `file` MUST still exist, and the store MUST refuse a `key_file` without a `file`.

title: A pattern rule is an obligation under a pattern
statement: A `pattern_rule` record MUST sit under a `pattern` and MUST be an obligation that needs proof only (LA-TRC-UC07-R06), proved by a test that `proves` it; a component MAY `satisfy` it. It MAY name, in its `setting` column, the one pattern setting it depends on.

title: Each domain that follows a pattern owes its rules
statement: Coverage MUST count each pattern rule once in each domain that follows its pattern, meaning the domain itself or one of its use cases `follows` the pattern, on that domain's `pattern_rule` line. A domain that does not follow the pattern MUST NOT count the rule, and the rule's gaps MUST name it in each domain that owes it.

title: A domain's own components and tests design and prove a pattern rule there
statement: In each domain that owes a pattern rule, the rule MUST count as proved only when an automated or manual test in that domain proves it, and planned when only a planned test there does.

title: A pattern rule does not apply where its setting is Not applicable
statement: When a pattern rule names a `setting`, the domain follows the pattern only through its use cases, and every one of them gives that setting a not-applicable reason (`setting_value.not_applicable`), the rule MUST NOT be counted in that domain. If any following use case there gives the setting a value, or the domain itself follows the pattern, the rule MUST be counted. A rule with no `setting` MUST be counted in every following domain.

title: Unsatisfied and unproved warnings name the pattern rule and the domain
statement: The `unproved` warning MUST report a pattern rule once for each domain that owes it and lacks the proof, with a message naming the rule and the domain, such as "Pattern rule TL-PAT-LIBRARIAN-ACTION-R01 is not proved in TL-LEND", and MUST say when the only test in that domain is planned.

title: A pattern rule naming a setting its pattern does not have is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a pattern rule whose `setting` or applies-when setting is not one of its pattern's `pattern_setting` names, as a foreign key naming the rule.

title: A pattern that no use case or domain follows is a warning
statement: When no use case and no domain follows a pattern, the engine MUST report a `pattern-not-followed` warning on the pattern, saying how many of its rules are therefore not counted in any domain.

title: Any other obligation outside every domain is a warning
statement: An obligation that sits in no domain, other than a pattern rule under a pattern, MUST be reported as an `obligation-outside-domain` warning, since no domain's coverage counts it.

title: A pattern rule no follower meets is waived in that domain
statement: A pattern rule with an applies-when setting MUST be owed in a domain only when at least one follower there (a use case that follows the pattern, or the domain when it follows the pattern itself) gives that setting a value, not a not-applicable reason, that meets it, compared trimmed and in any letter case. Elsewhere the rule MUST be waived: neither owed nor proved, so it adds nothing to that domain's coverage, gaps, `unproved` or `unsatisfied` warnings, and a test there that proves it proves nothing counted. A rule is owed only when not applicable by setting (LA-TRC-UC04-R04) does not take it away either.

title: A file that names the test's ID accepts all its claims
statement: When an automated test without a `key` has a `file` that names the test's own ID, the engine MUST report no claim of that test as unbacked.

title: Each proved ID the file leaves out is an error
statement: When an automated test without a `key` has a `file` that does not name the test's own ID, the engine MUST report one `proof-not-in-file` error on the test for each record the test proves whose ID the file does not name. The message MUST name the test, the proved ID and the file. The engine MUST NOT also report `test-file-missing-id` for that test.

title: A test's key must be in its file
statement: When an automated test has a non-empty `key`, the engine MUST report a `test-file-missing-id` error, quoting the key, if its `file` does not contain the key text exactly, and MUST NOT report `proof-not-in-file` for that test. If the file contains the key, the engine MUST report no claim of that test as unbacked.

title: A test that proves nothing still needs its ID in its file
statement: When an automated test without a `key` proves no record and its `file` does not name the test's own ID, the engine MUST report a `test-file-missing-id` error.

title: A manual or planned test's claims are not checked
statement: The engine MUST NOT report `proof-not-in-file` or `test-file-missing-id` for a manual or planned test.

title: Coverage counts every obligation a planned test is meant to prove
statement: Each obligation kind's coverage in a domain MUST report `planned_any`: how many of the domain's obligations of that kind a planned test is meant to prove, whether or not an automated or manual test already proves them. Two planned tests for one obligation MUST count it once. `planned` MUST keep counting only those not yet proved.

title: Coverage counts each domain's tests by state
statement: Each domain's coverage MUST report `tests`: how many test records sit in the domain with each state, `automated`, `manual` and `planned`, which every test gives. A domain with no tests MUST report zero of each.

title: lathe check reports owed proof and tests by state
statement: Each obligation line of `lathe check`'s coverage report MUST end with `; N/T with a planned test` where `planned_any` differs from `planned`, and with nothing more where they are equal. After a domain's obligation lines the report MUST print one line with its tests by state, such as `LA-CHK tests: 99 automated, 0 manual, 0 planned`.

title: A domain may follow a pattern and then owes every rule
statement: A `domain` MAY follow a pattern with the `follows` relation. Coverage MUST then count each of the pattern's rules in that domain, including a rule whose setting every following use case there marks Not applicable.

title: A domain follows a pattern itself or through any of its use cases
statement: Coverage and the `unsatisfied` and `unproved` checks MUST treat a domain as following a pattern when the domain or any of its use cases follows it, and MUST count each rule once there. When the domain follows only through its use cases, a rule whose setting all of them mark Not applicable MUST NOT be counted.

title: A pattern may have no settings
statement: A pattern MAY have no `pattern_setting` rows. A rule with no `setting` MUST apply wherever its pattern is followed, and `pattern-setting-missing` MUST ask only for the settings a pattern has.

title: An obligation kind may need proof only
statement: A kind's `meta_kind.obligation` MUST be `full` (an obligation), `proof` (an obligation that needs proof only) or `none`, a product's own kinds included, and the workspace MUST give each kind `obligation` and `proof_only` from it.

title: A proof-only obligation is counted for proof alone
statement: For a proof-only kind, coverage MUST report designed and built as equal to the total and give no `satisfies` gaps, and the `unsatisfied` warning MUST NOT fire. Proved, planned, planned_any and `proves` gaps MUST work as for any obligation.

title: Pattern rules need proof only, and a product cannot widen them
statement: The schema MUST mark `pattern_rule` as `proof`, and the store MUST refuse a product kind that takes the name of one of Lathe's tables, so a pattern rule asks for proof alone in every domain that owes it.

title: A use case that follows a pattern is not asked for requirements
statement: The `use-case-without-requirements` warning MUST NOT fire for a use case that follows a pattern.

title: Interaction requirements and flow steps may fulfill pattern rules
statement: The schema MUST allow `fulfills` from an `interaction_requirement` and from a `flow_step` to a `pattern_rule`.

title: A step may fulfill rules of the patterns its flow's use cases or domain follow
statement: `flow-step-fulfills-outside-flow` MUST treat as inside a flow the rules of the patterns that a use case the flow carries out, or the flow's domain, follows, and the interaction requirements that fulfill them; a step that fulfills any other pattern rule, or an interaction requirement that fulfills one, MUST be reported.

title: Each proved obligation a planned test still owes is named
statement: For each obligation that is proved and that a planned test is also meant to prove, the check MUST report a `proof-still-owed` warning naming the obligation and the planned test, such as `Requirement TL-LEND-UC01-R01 is proved, but planned test TL-LEND-T30 still owes a proof of it`. A pattern rule MUST be reported for each domain that owes it, naming that domain. An obligation not yet proved MUST NOT get this warning.

title: A test whose proof counts in no domain is reported
statement: A test that proves at least one record, none of whose proofs counts in any domain's coverage, MUST get a `proof-counts-nowhere` warning. The message MUST name each target with its reason: it is not an obligation, it sits in no domain, it is a pattern rule owed only by other domains, or it is a pattern rule no domain owes (no use case follows its pattern, or wherever it is followed the rule's setting is Not applicable or no follower meets its `applies_when`).

title: A manual test whose file never mentions it is reported
statement: A manual test whose `file` exists but names neither the test's ID, nor any ID it proves, nor its `key` MUST get a `manual-test-file-silent` warning naming the test and the file. Automated and planned tests MUST NOT get this warning.

title: The product page shows each domain with its coverage
statement: The product page MUST show each domain as a card, linking to the domain page, with its coverage of requirements and of domain rules as small bars with counts.

title: The product page lists its open questions and problems
statement: The product page MUST list the product's open questions, with their owners, and the problems found in its records.

title: The product page sums up what Lathe counts across the product
statement: The product page MUST show, in a Summary section, what Lathe counts across the product's domains: its coverage (designed, built, proved and planned), its tests by state, its open questions, and its errors and warnings. A product with nothing to count MUST show zeros, not an empty section.

title: Coverage shows designed, built and proved counts
statement: Wherever coverage appears, it MUST show designed, built, proved and planned counts for each obligation kind, as `LA-TRC-UC11-R01` details.

title: Trace mode shows only the traceability chain and its files
statement: In trace mode the graph MUST show only the requirement or rule, the flows, views and endpoints that fulfill it, the components that satisfy it or implement those views and endpoints, the tests that prove it, and the files those components and tests name.

title: Trace mode is offered only for requirements and domain rules
statement: The trace mode switch MUST be offered when the focused record is a requirement or a domain rule, and MUST NOT be offered for any other kind.

title: Coverage shows one group per obligation kind
statement: Wherever coverage appears (the product page's domain cards and the domain page), it MUST show one group of bars per obligation kind the engine reports, labeled with the kind's label, each with designed, built, proved and planned counts.

title: The summary counts every obligation kind
statement: The product's Summary MUST total designed, built and proved over every obligation kind, and MUST show the planned count on its own line, apart from proved.

title: Interaction requirements are listed under their view, endpoint or flow
statement: The domain page MUST list each interaction requirement, and each record of an obligation kind a product adds, nested under the view, endpoint or flow it belongs to, with its gaps and problems on its row. Searching for one MUST keep its view, endpoint or flow shown above it.

title: Each test shows its state
statement: The domain page MUST tag each test with its state (automated, manual or planned), and the record page MUST show a test's state. A planned test MUST look unfinished on both pages, and the record page MUST say it does not count as proof.

title: The record page shows what an interaction requirement fulfills
statement: For an interaction requirement, the record page MUST show the view, endpoint or flow it sits at and each requirement or domain rule it fulfills, with its kind. When it fulfills nothing, the page MUST say so and how to link it.

title: The record content can sit inside another view
statement: A record's content (header, typed fields, parts, parent, children and links) MUST be one piece that takes a record ID and an `onNavigate` callback, apart from the page around it, so the graph can show it beside itself. Links inside it MUST go through `onNavigate` on a plain click and stay real links otherwise. It SHOULD read well at half the screen width.

title: Every list stays at 10 rows and can be searched
statement:
Every list in the spec pages (the menu's domains, a domain's record groups and nested lists, coverage gaps, problems and checks, open questions, a record's children and links both ways) MUST show up to 10 items as a plain list. With more than 10 it MUST show the first 10 rows' height and scroll inside, with a search box above it that filters by ID and title, a count such as "12 of 48", and a clear message when nothing matches.

The search box MUST be reachable with Tab, Escape MUST clear it, and the scrolling area MUST take focus so it scrolls from the keyboard. The list MUST know nothing about specs, so other views can use it.

title: A domain page lists the patterns it follows
statement: A domain page MUST have a "Patterns we follow" section listing each pattern that the domain itself follows ("followed by the whole domain", with every rule applying) or that any of its use cases follows, with the use cases that follow it. Each pattern's rules MUST be folded under its row, one level deep like the rest of the page, and each rule MUST show whether this domain designs it (a component in the domain satisfies it), builds it (that component's file exists) and proves it (an automated or manual test in the domain proves it), with planned proof shown apart. A domain that follows no pattern MUST say so.

title: A rule the domain marks not applicable says so, with the use case and reason
statement: When a pattern rule names a setting and every use case in the domain that follows the pattern gives that setting a not-applicable reason, the rule MUST show as not applicable in that domain instead of designed, built and proved, naming each use case (as a link) and its reason.

title: A pattern page shows its settings, rules and followers
statement: A pattern's page (`/<id>`) MUST show a settings table (each setting and the rules that depend on it), its rules, and each domain that follows it with that domain's following use cases, the value each gives for each setting, and the domain's status for each rule as on the domain page. A pattern nobody follows MUST say that no domain owes its rules. The rules MUST NOT be listed a second time as plain children.

title: A pattern rule page shows the domains that owe it
statement: A pattern rule's page MUST list each domain that follows its pattern, with that domain's status for the rule (designed, built, proved, planned, or not applicable with the reasons).

title: Coverage counts pattern rules per domain
statement: A domain's coverage MUST show the `pattern_rule` line the engine reports for it (total, designed, built, proved, planned), and its coverage gaps MUST name each pattern rule the domain does not yet satisfy or prove.

title: A waived rule says Waived here, with the value the domain gives
statement: Where a pattern rule is waived in a domain, the domain page, the pattern page and the pattern rule page MUST show it there as "Waived here: <setting> is <value>", naming the value or values that domain's followers give the setting (or "not given"), instead of designed, built and proved, and the rule's Traceability gaps MUST leave that domain out. A rule's row MUST say what it applies when.

title: The planned bar shows proof still owed beyond the unproved
statement: Where the engine reports `planned_any` greater than `planned` for an obligation kind, the planned bar MUST say `N more planned`, N being the difference, with a hover text saying those are already proved but still have a planned test. Where they are equal, nothing more MUST be shown.

title: Each domain's coverage shows its tests by state
statement: Each domain's coverage, on the product page's domain cards and on the domain page, MUST show its tests by state, such as `Tests 12 automated, 1 manual, 2 planned`, from `Coverage.tests`.

title: The summary totals the product's tests and its owed proof
statement: The product's Summary MUST show a `Tests` row totalling its domains' tests by state, and its `Planned` row MUST add `; N more planned beside proof` when proof is still owed for obligations already proved.

title: An obligation lists what designs, proves, supports and carries it out
statement: An obligation's record page MUST show a Traceability section after its text and before its children, with these groups in this order, each left out when empty: Designed by (its incoming `design`-role links, each component marked built or not built), Proved by (its incoming `proof`-role links, each test with its state), Supported by, Carried out in, Applied by, then its other incoming links under their reverse labels, then its links out under their forward labels, such as the aggregates a domain rule involves. An interaction requirement's links out to what it carries out MUST NOT be repeated there, since its own Carries out section shows them.

title: Each gap shows as a callout linked to its check
statement: An obligation's Traceability MUST name each gap in a callout: "Not designed yet" when its kind needs design and nothing designs it, "Not built yet" when no designing component's file exists, and "Not proved yet" when nothing proves it, saying when its test is only planned. Each callout MUST link to the page of the check that reports it (`unsatisfied`, `component-file-missing`, `unproved`). A pattern rule MUST show one line for each domain that owes it.

title: A use case shows its requirements in a table
statement: A use case's Traceability MUST show a table with one row per UC requirement and the columns Requirement, Designed, Built and Proved, each cell linking the records that design, build or prove it and flagging a gap, followed by Carried out by flow, Follows and Applies, each applied rule with its own coverage marks.

title: A component and a test show what they design, prove and run from
statement: A component's Traceability MUST show Satisfies (what it designs), then Proved through (the tests proving those things, rolled up), then its other links under their labels. A test's MUST show Proves and Supports, then the file that runs it with its state, flagged when the file is missing. Any other kind MUST show its links out under their forward labels and its links in under their reverse labels.

title: Every link is shown by its label
statement: The record facts beside the body, the side bar's Links out and Links in, the graph's edge labels, legend and connections, and the Model view's line titles MUST name links by their relation's `forward_label` (from the source) or `reverse_label` (from the target), never by the relation's code.

title: Domain events show what raises them and what reacts to them
statement: An aggregate's page MUST list its domain events in their own list titled "Domain events" (LA-EXP-DR36), each row one link to the event saying which entity raises it and how many records react to it, and its list of other children MUST NOT list them again. An event's page MUST show its fields (its `event_field` rows), as an entity's page shows its `entity_field` rows, and its Traceability MUST list "Raised by" and "Reacted to by"; a record that reacts to an event MUST list it under "Reacts to". Every one of these words MUST come from the relations' labels in the schema.
